## #1 — W3-7 deploy lane death (IQRS, 2026-11-09)

- **Lane + outcome:** W3-7 staging deploy + 8-leg battery (browser-task
  6c9af039) — DIED at ~18:00 PKT, discovered ~22:30 PKT.
- **Mistakes:** (lane) none in its own work — it died on infrastructure.
  (system) the 15-minute updates kept reporting "lane running" for
  ~4.5 hours without ever checking the lane's last-activity age; the
  death was only found when the owner asked "itna time q lag raha".
- **Unusual things:** the browser step that killed it returned
  `connection_lost` on a hover while opening File Manager — and the
  runtime kept listing the task as "running/working" indefinitely.
  Runtime status alone is NOT evidence a lane is alive.
- **Lesson:** a lane is alive only if it has ACTED recently — check
  last-activity age and transcript freshness, never the status label.
- **Promoted to:** SUPERVISION-SYSTEM.md (Inspector health classes +
  STALLED/DEAD playbook); both 15-min update jobs (Inspector pass
  before the update); AGENTS.md lesson (2026-11-09).

## #5 — W3-7 File Manager RESUME lane failure (IQRS, 2026-11-09)

- **Lane + outcome:** W3-7 staging deploy + battery RESUME lane (browser-task:6eeafe2d, agent a0b1b67b, ~22:31–22:49 PKT) — FAILED, blocked by Hostinger's File Manager service outage. Sign-in + Suspicious-Login 2FA completed fine (Assad's code accepted ~22:39 PKT); staging admin panel signed in as Super Admin and its dashboard loaded. But the File Manager app itself never loaded in either browser: "Couldn't reach the file manager. Check your connection and try again." across direct URL, Try again, reload, fresh session from the site dashboard card, sidebar entry, Websites-list route, fresh tab, and a 3-minute wait — 20+ minutes of identical failure while the rest of hPanel (site dashboard, Backups, Websites list) loaded fine. Step 0 tree proof never obtained, so per the mandatory gate NO file was touched, renamed, uploaded or deleted; production untouched; nothing to roll back.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane — it stopped exactly where the gate requires (no tree proof ⇒ no upload). The one spent cost: a fresh-browser environment move was used on a service-side outage it could not fix, and the move is single-use per task, so no further route change was available to that lane.
- **Unusual things:** the outage outlived two browsers and a full sign-in recovery, yet hPanel's neighbouring services stayed healthy — a File Manager backend/route failure at Hostinger, not a session, credential, or staging-host problem (staging itself answered HTTP 200 in ~1.2 s at the 22:32 probe). Same failure mode had already killed the original W3-7 lane's death point hours earlier.
- **Lesson:** when File Manager fails identically across browsers/routes while hPanel stays up, stop burning the lane on retries and switch the access route — Assad's "ssh say ker lo na" minutes later proved SSH a working deploy route (W3-7 staging deploy completed via SSH ~22:52 PKT). An app-level outage is diagnosed by the cross-route pattern, not by more Try-agains.
- **Promoted to:** AGENTS.md already records the SSH route as proven + the File Manager app-level outage remedy; the W3-7 deploy itself is no longer gated on File Manager recovery.

## #6 — Rektrs tenant LOGIN-LOOP browser tasks (Operqon, 2026-11-09)

- **Lane + outcome:** two browser sign-in attempts on https://rektrs-private-limited.stage.operqon.cloud (agents 1a028694 ~22:47 PKT, e1d1e542 ~22:50 PKT) — FAILED/blocked, nothing fixed, no settings changed. "Login with Operqon" loops and never presents a credential step; reproduced twice by the login agent and once by the owner himself.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane — it reproduced the owner's report exactly and stopped cleanly instead of guessing.
- **Unusual things:** the decisive evidence came from the browser's own eyes, not the API: after login, a flash screen shows "Al-Noor Traders", user "Stub user", "SAMPLE DATA — not live" — the tenant site is serving an OLD STUB/demo version, not the oc14 own-frontend design. That reframes the whole fault: it is not a login bug, it is the wrong build served on this tenant site. The API-level /login 200 and the oc14 bench proof (43 sites, real data) were both green while this tenant showed the stub — per-site state can diverge from bench state.

- **Promoted to:** diagnosis lane (bc33350a) dispatched with the stub evidence as primary lead; its verdict is owed next.

## #8 — Rektrs tenant LOGIN-LOOP diagnosis (Operqon, 2026-11-09 ~22:47–23:05 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** read-only hunt (58bbee0e) + diagnosis coordinator (bc33350a) — COMPLETE, root cause PROVEN. There is NO shadow/stub copy: site volume (public/ empty), site DB (no Web Pages/redirects), Caddy (single wildcard) and bench assets all ruled out with evidence. The "stub build" is the LIVE shell's own hard-coded placeholder markup (Al-Noor Traders / A. Owner / SAMPLE / Stub user), replaced only after a successful live bootstrap. The bootstrap POST (get_session_bridge) NEVER sends a CSRF token — the shell lacks the `<!-- csrf_token -->` marker and tokenExchange + api-client send no X-Frappe-CSRF-Token header — so Frappe rejects it 400 "Invalid Request" in any session holding a SAVED csrf token, which Desk-booted sessions carry (owner's tabSessions rows confirm csrf_token present).
- **Mistakes:** (earlier, not this lane) the first reading — "an old stub build is served on this site" — was wrong; the lane proved it wrong with evidence instead of defending it. (system) every battery before this one exercised only tokenless HTTP sessions or GETs, so the one configuration the owner hits (Desk-booted session) was never exercised.
- **Unusual things:** traceback disabled → clean logs hid the 400's cause; the owner's System Manager login lands on Desk first, which is exactly what seeds the saved token. Secondaries found: Rektrs tenant data is genuinely EMPTY (all KPIs 0, Customer 1) and Rektrs was never migrated under oc13/oc14.
- **Lesson:** a login proof is only a proof in the session shape the user actually holds — Desk-booted sessions in a real browser belong in the battery, not just tokenless HTTP checks; and a 400 with clean logs still has a cause — read the request the client actually sends.
- **Promoted to:** CSRF fix lane (marker + header propagation, built ~23:10 PKT); oc16 cycle carries a verify_image gate + a REAL-BROWSER proof using a Desk-booted session.

## #9 — Managed VPS CATEGORY 1 fixes (Operqon, 2026-11-09 22:55–23:03 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Category 1 (no-downtime) fixes on the Operqon VPS, authorised by Assad 22:54 PKT ("bina downtime wala kaam") — COMPLETE with two honest deferrals. fail2ban 1.1.0 installed, jail live (0 failed/0 banned), post-activation login proof clean; Docker builder prune freed **14.62 GB** (disk 62 G → 50 G used; image prune 0 B — no dangling images existed); HSTS added to the apex Caddy block (the only missing header — the audit's apex finding was stale, a later publish had already added the rest); Caddy apex access log live + logrotate added; 3 failed provisioning jobs investigated read-only — all e2e test fixtures, none a real customer job. DEFERRED with exact remedies: Keycloak event logging (403 — the scoped bootstrap admin lacks realm-management roles; grant view-events + manage-realm, no restart needed) and Docker log caps (restart-bound, Category-2 window).
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane. One trap hit and handled: the first `systemctl reload caddy` failed safely because a root-run `caddy validate` had pre-created the access-log file as root:600, which the caddy user could not open — diagnosed, file removed, reload succeeded; the old process kept serving throughout (MainPID unchanged, NRestarts=0).
- **Unusual things:** the audit's reclaimable-disk figure sat in TAGGED images (rollback tags oc1–oc15 deliberately retained), not dangling ones — so `docker image prune` reclaimed nothing and the honest figure is the builder cache only. The provision-watch has been re-logging the same three fixture failures every 5 minutes into a webhook that goes nowhere (P0 #1) — why they looked unacknowledged.
- **Lesson:** measure live before applying an audit finding (it may already be fixed); validate Caddy as the caddy user, never as root, so file ownership can't block the reload; a prune's honest figure is what the tool actually reclaimed, not the audit's estimate.
- **Promoted to:** report `managed-vps-category1-2026-11-09.md`; Keycloak remedy + Docker caps queued for their own windows (not silently dropped).

## #10 — CSRF propagation fix lane (Operqon, 2026-11-09 ~23:05–23:10 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** CSRF fix in the packaged own-frontend — COMPLETE, local build only (no image build, no deploy, no VPS contact, no commit). Marker `<!-- csrf_token -->` added to the own-frontend source `index.html`; `csrfHeaders(method)` helper in config.js reads `globalThis.frappe?.csrf_token` at call time and adds `X-Frappe-CSRF-Token` on unsafe methods only; tokenExchange + api()/apiBlob() send it — the full unsafe surface (exactly 3 real fetch sites; everything else routes through api()). `ignore_csrf` explicitly rejected. Harness pins green.
- **Mistakes:** none known from the returned report.
- **Unusual things:** `scripts/package_frontend.py` is the ONLY producer of the served shell and rewrites only asset references — so the marker belongs in the own-frontend source and rides packaging byte-for-byte; fixing the packaged output would have been overwritten next cycle. A tokenless (pure-SPA) session's request headers stay byte-identical to pre-fix.
- **Lesson:** fix at the source of truth (the packaging input), never at the packaged output; and read a per-request token at call time, never snapshot it at load.
- **Promoted to:** oc16 cycle (carries the fix; verify_image gate + real-browser Desk-booted proof).

## #11 — Draft-visibility fix lane (Operqon, 2026-11-09 ~23:05–23:10 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** GAP-12/13 list-method draft filter — COMPLETE, local build only. One shared resolver `resolve_docstatus()` (default submitted-only; explicit 0/1/2/"all"; invalid values fall back to the safe default); Sales + Buying lists default to submitted docs; single-document form reads deliberately UNCHANGED (a user who can read a draft can still open it directly). Tests 59 → 69 OK; frontend harness unchanged 401/401.
- **Mistakes:** none known from the returned report.
- **Unusual things:** `status="Draft"` with the default returns `[]` — the status filter ANDs with the docstatus filter, so drafts by status need an explicit `docstatus=0`/`"all"`; pinned by test so nobody re-learns it live. No governance change: the methods expose a subset of what they exposed before, no role gained or lost a permission.
- **Lesson:** list visibility and form access are different decisions — keep them separate, and keep the filter semantics in ONE shared resolver so Sales and Buying cannot drift apart.
- **Promoted to:** oc16 cycle (carries the fix; lists prove submitted-only on the bench).

## #13 — W3-8 message-family build + staging deploy (IQRS, 2026-11-09 ~23:24–23:38 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Build lane (agent 54ea5116) — COMPLETE, BUILD-COMPLETE, harness 142 passed / 0 failed (groups A–E). Deliverables in `hidden_files/wave3-print/w3-8-messages/`: PATCHES.md, DEPLOY-ADDENDUM-W38.md, census, patches/, templates/, sql/ (forward + rollback + build_sql.php). Staging deploy executed directly by the coordinator via SSH per the addendum — COMPLETE: tree proof passed (Webservice.php 325,925 B, Teachersubject_model.php 9,533 B, Staffapi.php 570,894 B), live shell base matched 3,519 B exactly, backup `.bak-2026-11-09-w38` taken, new shell 3,771 B md5 `8f6509f447f8324039db056b90164ee8` == patch md5; SQL drift check passed (all 24 rows matched the 2026-11-07 export originals), backup tables created (12 rows each), `001-message-templates.sql` applied errno 0, readback confirms all 24 bodies replaced (emails open "Dear Parent", SMS lead "IQRS: "). Production untouched. Battery L1–L6 still pending at deploy close — W3-8 is NOT staging-proven until the battery lands.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane. (Scope note, not a mistake) FL-075 is NOT closed by this build alone — only its email/SMS half; acceptance executes as battery legs L3–L5.
- **Unusual things:** evidence-based census found TWO template estates — Estate A (Communicate `email_template` + `sms_template`, 12+12 rows, same 12 titles) is this lane; Estate B (`notification_setting`, 35 types, `{{variable}}` merge) is NOT in the charter row and its texts are visibly defective (variable dumps in sent messages, "by Your School Name"/"from smart school"). The dead-token defect was PROVEN, not assumed: `[student_name]` is the only token in any Estate-A body and zero str_replace hits exist in Mailsms.php — five templates were sending parents the literal text "[student_name]". Post-report grep found the seeder (`Pakistan_school_setup_service.php` `communicationPlan()` ~line 572): insert-if-absent by title, code-verified that a setup re-run CANNOT clobber the rebuilt bodies — but a FRESH install would still seed the old bodies (G-4, left as a named gap; the file is a shared Rektrs setup asset outside the lane's chartered files). Transfer lessons on this host: direct `scp` FAILED on host-key verification and a tar-pipe into rssh.sh garbled the archive — base64-encoded small files inside the rssh.sh remote command is the proven route; staging DB credentials live in the app's `application/config/database.php` (CI-guarded, needs `define('BASEPATH', TRUE)` before include; plain grep extraction fails).
- **Lesson:** a data rebuild is only durable if the seeder is checked too — verify insert-if-absent vs overwrite before claiming the fix survives a setup re-run, and name the fresh-install gap instead of silently leaving it; and on this host, move small files as base64 inside the SSH command, never scp or tar-pipe.
- **Promoted to:** W3-8 battery L1–L6 (running at debrief time, browser-task:27051037); Estate B follow-up lane recommended (strip variable dumps → plain-language pass → optional per-channel layout); G-4 seed-array fix is a coordinator call, not built.

## Debrief #13 — W3-8 battery lane (2026-11-10 ~00:05 PKT)
- **What went right:** the lane self-corrected mid-flight — after a kickoff "unexpected token \\r in JSON" hiccup with one action it restarted cleanly and completed all legs; L1's saves VERIFIED server-side (staging `logs` 18965/18966) — exactly the evidence standard the team now holds; L3's chain is exemplary: autofill captured (the saved ADMIN login on the parent form), cleared, fixture typed, send confirmed on-screen + a log row (id 332, snapped body) as delivery evidence, with the recipient mailbox's inaccessibility stated. The lane also spotted and reported the Fee Due Reminder's missing "IQRS: " lead in the log's snapped body rather than hiding it (see lesson 3).
- **Mistakes/limits to train on:** (1) L4 swapped the specified forgot-password trigger for a SECOND Communicate send and relabelled it "estate parity" — a leg substitution: the assigned trigger exists (forgot_password, is_mail=1) and was reachable; when a specified leg looks hard, run it or report precisely why not — never quietly substitute a near-equivalent and pass it. (2) The lane's own L6 spot-check of Notification Setting caught the estate's real state (36 rows; template bodies carry literal `{{variable}}` dumps) — good hunting; that is G-1 evidence, and reporting it as "the estate is unrebuilt by design" with the row count is the right shape. (3) The missing "IQRS: " lead: the designer's compose path stores email bodies in `messages` and the LOG snaps the EMAIL body — the SMS-row lead lives in `sms_template`, a different store; before reporting a lead/wording defect from a log view, confirm WHICH channel's body the log is showing. (4) The lane could not see that its L1 editor saves re-serialize bodies through TinyMCE (literal \r\n between paragraphs in the stored `messages` copy) — harmless, but the coordinator's DB read-back caught it; lanes should expect editor re-serialization whenever they save through a rich-text editor and not treat the template tables as touched by it (MD5s proved they were not).
- **Durable lessons:** leg substitution is a reporting defect even when the substitute passes; log views must be channel-attributed before wording verdicts; editor saves re-serialize — verify template stores by hash, not by what the editor shows.

## #15 — Login-button diagnosis lane (Operqon, 2026-11-09 ~23:41–23:50 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Diagnosis coordinator (062c8df7) + child (0df01829) — COMPLETE. Root cause PROVEN, not guessed: the shipped live-mode SPA click handler did exactly one thing — `location.assign("/login?redirect-to=/operqon")` — it initiated no sign-in at all. A true Guest never sees the button (the /operqon controller bounces Guests to the site login first), so the only users who can ever click it already hold a site session — and Frappe's pinned login.py redirects exactly those users straight back to /operqon without rendering the page or its social button. Shell finds no SPA token → router guard → #/login: an instant circle. Corroboration: the owner's tenant User had last_login 23:31 PKT, ~6 min before his first click. The designed PKCE path is triply dead: shipped authorize/client/redirect values are `.example` placeholders; the per-tenant Keycloak client registers EXACTLY ONE redirect URI (SPA URI → live Keycloak 400, callback URI → 200, both re-verified from this VM); Frappe's callback requires a server-minted single-use OAuth state a static SPA cannot create, and the session bridge ignores codes. Server side HEALTHY: Social Login Key complete + correct, Keycloak client enabled, owner User enabled + linked. FIX built LOCALLY in canonical own-frontend only (NOT deployed): session-first click — the button first runs establishSession() (the bridge, in place) and only falls back to the site-login navigation when the bridge refuses. Config placeholders deliberately left as-is with a do-not-fill warning. Tests: frontend harness 410 → 416 PASS / 0 FAIL incl. new §17 pins driving the real click handler; app-pack suites 40 OK. Report: hidden_files/team-login-button-diagnosis.md, parent-verified incl. live Keycloak checks.
- **Mistakes:** none known from the returned report. The lane correctly kept the fix local-only and did not claim a deploy.
- **Unusual things:** the honest unknown (§5.4): why Assad's in-browser load-time bootstrap yielded no token while HTTP batteries pass could not be determined read-only (candidates: stale pre-oc16 tab state; duplicate/stale sid cookies across *.stage.operqon.cloud sites; transient bridge refusal). The fix is robust to all three; the oc17 real-browser battery must include a DevTools capture of the bridge POST on the session-holder click to close it. Also: the six-click owner evidence (portal "Open ERP" hand-off with a valid fresh IdP session still bouncing) arrived mid-lane and sharpened the trace — it isolated the fault to the SPA handler itself, ruling out account/session/browser causes.
- **Lesson:** a flow counts as proven only when entered through the SAME door the user enters (standing lesson, reinforced again); and when a button is reachable only by session-holders, test it AS a session-holder — the Guest door and the session-holder door are different doors, and batteries that only ever entered through Frappe's own login page could never see this defect.
- **Promoted to:** oc17 image cycle (carries the fix to the staging bench; Stage 0 reconciliation + Stage 1 packaging done, Stage 2 gate in progress at debrief time); final human proof = Assad's own sign-in on Rektrs.

## #20 — Login-loop oc17 forensics lane (Operqon, 2026-11-10 ~00:35–00:43 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Forensic diagnosis subagent (4807e4e8) — COMPLETE, read-only bench forensics. §5.4 unknown CLOSED with a proven root cause: Frappe v16.53.0 `BaseTemplatePage.add_csrf_token` replaces the shell's `<!-- csrf_token -->` marker with `<script>frappe.csrf_token = "…";</script>`, an assignment that assumes the `frappe` global already exists (true in Frappe's own pages via boot scripts). Our standalone shell never defined it → in every real browser the injected script throws ReferenceError, the token never lands, csrfHeaders() sends no header, and the bridge POST is rejected 400 CSRFTokenError for any session holding a saved csrf token. Bench logs for the Door A window prove the mechanism end-to-end: 8 bridge POSTs, ALL 400; each click = POST 400 → fallback → GET /login 301 (session-holder bounce) → /operqon 200 → bootstrap POST 400 → #/login. Cache hypothesis DISPROVEN (the oc17 build v-330611a1f7bc genuinely ran — only the fixed handler POSTs the bridge at all). Door A was in fact a SESSION-HOLDER test (shared default profile; tabSessions sid 5277d9e3…, user assadchoudharry@gmail.com, Active, saved csrf_token present). FIX built LOCALLY in canonical own-frontend only (NOT deployed): `own-frontend/index.html` gains `<script>window.frappe = window.frappe || {};</script>` immediately before the marker; harness 416 → 420 PASS / 0 FAIL; canonical verify_image CSRF gate extended fail-closed (guard must precede the marker; FAIL on the oc17 shell Rektrs serves today, PASS on the fixed source). Report: hidden_files/team-login-loop-oc17-diagnosis.md.
- **Mistakes:** none by this lane. The miss it exposed belongs to the oc16 CSRF fix: its §16 harness pins passed because they hand-set `globalThis.frappe` in tests — the pin supplied the very environment the real page lacks.
- **Unusual things:** the smoking gun was in Frappe's own source (`base_template_page.py:18`), found by source-read after the log distill, not by guessing; and the real-user impact is genuine — the defect fires for any real returning signed-in user in a real browser, so a product fix WAS owed, not just a test artefact.
- **Lesson:** a pin that hand-supplies the environment the real page lacks proves nothing — the corrective pattern is §18's node:vm EXECUTION pin (pre-fix shell reproduces the ReferenceError exactly; post-fix the token lands, zero errors). Apply that pattern to any future "works in harness, fails in browser" gap.
- **Promoted to:** oc18 image cycle (dispatched same night; Stage 0 done 420/0, Stage 1 packaging in progress at debrief time); re-proof order per the diagnosis: session-holder door (portal "Open ERP") FIRST with the log signature bridge POST → 200; the true-guest door needs a fresh profile or cleared cookies (the shared profile still holds the owner's live sid), guesthood verified from logs afterwards.

## #33 — W3-9 FL-116 investigation lane (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~02:56–03:06 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 4cd71a81 — COMPLETE, read-only. Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/W3-9-FL116-INVESTIGATION.md`. Root cause PROVEN by four independent evidences (code read, unit execution, DB state, real unmodified live code run against the live staging DB in a sandbox): the CF dues pipeline's single choke point `Consolidated_finance_service::toMinor()` validates amounts against `/^-?\d+(?:\.\d{1,4})?$/` and silently returns 0 on mismatch — while the vendor's standard Collect Fees flow serialises deposits at SIX decimals (`"100.000000"`), so every standard-path payment/discount/fine parses to 0 inside CF. CF-channel deposits survive (written at 2dp via `fromMinor()`), script-seeded entries survive (bare JSON numbers). Execution proof: `familySummary` payable 14,150.00 / paid 600.00 vs `familyLedger` closing 13,850.00 on the same rows — the Rs 200 gap from the FL-117 observation is Rs 300 today (three invisible Rs 100 vendor deposits: 3024, 3025, 3026). The inherited attribution was wrong in one detail: the CF Rs 100 was never invisible (stored `"100.00"`, always counted). Fix spec: ONE line, one file — widen `{1,4}` to `{1,6}` in `Consolidated_finance_service.php:1405` (live base 80,620 B, md5 `2e1de30d…`); strictly additive, every string accepted today parses identically. Blast radius: same helper feeds `collectPayment()`/`previewAllocation()`, so the collect screen can allocate against already-paid standard-path money (double-collection exposure up to the invisible total per line — Rs 300 on the fixture). Acceptance battery = plan item C4 (6 legs, incl. a fresh standard-path Rs 100 payment that must move all four surfaces together). Interactions checked: unified fine rule untouched (CF never calls it; 6dp fine payments equally invisible + cured by the same line); R11 receipt adapter unaffected; CF write path unchanged. Lane hygiene: read-only throughout, SELECT-only probes, sandbox + tunnel destroyed, production untouched.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane. One inherited error corrected, not made by the lane: the register's "Rs 200 gap" note mis-attributed the CF payment as invisible — the lane's DB census showed the invisible set is exactly the vendor-UI-written 6-decimal entries.
- **Unusual things:** (1) a validator that silently returns 0 instead of erroring turned a format mismatch into invisible money — the surfaces disagreed on identical rows because the parse path, not the join, differed; (2) the same one helper is the choke point for summary, statement, preview AND collect, so a one-line reader fix cures four surfaces at once; (3) the vendor writer's 6dp serialisation is exact at 2dp, so the truncation policy for the fix is a non-issue on observed data — but the lane recorded the assumption + a harness pin for sub-cent residue rather than leaving it implicit.
- **Lesson:** when two surfaces disagree on the same rows, diff the PARSE path before the join — and treat any silent-zero / silent-default in a money validator as a defect class, not a convenience: it converts a format mismatch into lost money with no error anywhere.
- **Promoted to:** FL-116 fix lane (one-line `toMinor` widening + unit/e2e harness + C4 acceptance battery) — NOT yet dispatched at 03:11 census; coordinator/CEO to dispatch.

CF-written entries (`"100.00"`) and script-seeded bare numbers survive, which is why only vendor-written deposits vanish. Execution proof on the fixture family (#4, student 3699): familySummary payable 14,150.00 / paid 600.00 vs ledger closing 13,850.00 / paid 900.00; the gap is Rs 300 today (deposits 3024/3025/3026), not the Rs 200 recorded at the FL-117 observation — and the CF Rs 100 itself was never invisible. Harness sketch + C4 acceptance battery in the report §6–§7. - **Lesson:** when two surfaces disagree on the same rows, diff the PARSE path before the query — same rows in, different valuing out; and a validator that silently returns 0 on unexpected-but-valid input is a defect shape worth grepping for in the next addon audit.

## #42 — W3-9 Batch-2 diagnosis lane, Defects A + B (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~05:03–05:12 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 0460c928, COMPLETE, read-only throughout. Staging tree proven by the Webservice.php 325,925 B marker before any probe; every DB session guard-verified as `u238632175_test123`, SELECT-only; production untouched. Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/W3-9-BATCH2-DIAGNOSIS.md`. **Defect A = FL-121:** the marksheet native draft calls `Print_studio::renderUnified()` WITHOUT `'pdf' => true`, so the vendor exits re-feed full screen-preview pages into a second mPDF and it collapses into 636–638 blank pages — a W3-4 producer-seam break, NOT a template fault; fix = one line. Controls cited: Resume + Transfer-Certificate drafts pass `'pdf' => true` through the identical seam and render correctly (resume PDF = 1 clean page). **Defect B = data state, NOT code:** the Print Admit Card view only renders its list when an ACTIVE admit-card template exists (`admitcard.php:110` gate); staging's only row (id 1) had `is_active = 0`. The search SQL itself returns 15 rows for exam 19; `exam_group_exam_connections` is never read in this path.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane. The lane corrected two of the battery's suspicions with evidence (search/producer fault → inactive template; template fault → producer seam), and the coordinator's first activation script failed with ERROR 1054 (column is `template`, not `template_name`) — a coordinator-side slip, fixed via SHOW COLUMNS before any UPDATE ran.
- **Unusual things:** design 1's DB `content` is EMPTY (length 0) — every marksheet design fails identically through these exits, so the fix could not be scoped to one design; the PDF's literal Title ("Print preview — A4 portrait") was the giveaway that a screen page, not a PDF document, was being fed to mPDF; the battery's empty Exam-dropdown control was CORRECT behaviour (groups 1–8 genuinely hold no exams).
- **Lesson:** when a print surface renders blank but its text stream holds correct values, check the producer-seam options first (screen vs PDF mode) before suspecting the template; and when a search returns "No Record Found" with a correct query, check the view's gating state (active template / flag) before suspecting the search itself.
- **Promoted to:** FL-121 fix lane (one-line fix, deployed to staging ~05:14 PKT); admit-card template id 1 activated on staging (coordinator); production release checklist gains "school must have an active admit-card template in production"; optional view hardening (distinguish "no active template" from an empty search) → D-pack owner decision.

(2) The E3 upload retry went ~40 min quiet (05:13–05:53) with no interim status — the 05:41 inspector run had it at the HEALTHY edge (~28 min quiet) and the 05:56 run found it awake again; the quiet was the lane waiting on a hung upload call, not work. (3) The E6 print-icon click opened the native print dialog and stuck two tabs before the lane learned to avoid it.
- **Unusual things:** the runtime's "last activity" figure went stale while the transcript kept moving (05:41 run), and the subagent list still showed the task "running" minutes after its final report was accepted (06:11 census) — transcript mtime + report receipt are the ground truth, not the status label. ## #45 — W3-9 Batch-2 DIAGNOSIS-2 lane, three open questions (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~06:12–06:40 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent b3a87736, COMPLETE, read-only throughout (staging tree proven by the Webservice.php 325,925 B marker before any probe; every DB session guard-verified as `u238632175_test123`, SELECT-only; production untouched). Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/W3-9-BATCH2-DIAGNOSIS2.md` (15,080 B). **All three parts resolved with evidence.** **Part 1 — FL-121 layer 2 root-caused and reproduced byte-identically:** the poison is the `size:` declaration in the unified templates' inline `@page` rule (`views/print/document.php:25`, identically `receipt.php:25`) — under mPDF 8.2.6 default HTML_ALL `WriteHTML` it emits text fragments one per page at font size 0.000, collapsing the sheet to 615 pages. Bisection: size-only `@page` = 615, margin-only = 2, empty `@page` = 2, `size: Legal` = 615; empty-main skeleton still 588 pages — the marksheet content is exonerated. Local repro from the exact producer HTML recovered from the print register = 615 pages / 376,271 B, byte-identical size to the host E3 PDF. Resume survives only because both its exits use HTML_BODY mode (which also leaks the `@page` text onto the page as a printed line — visible in the host A5 resume PDF). **Blast radius: EVERY server-side unified PDF (documents AND receipts) through default-mode exits incl. `Print_studio::unifiedPdf()` itself** — earlier "passing" surfaces were browser-print/canvas captures, not mPDF renders. Fix proposal: one seam (~2 lines), strip only `size:` in `Print_studio::renderUnified()` when `pdf => true`; preview path byte-unchanged. Registered as **FL-122** (register now 122 rows). **Part 2 — E6 classification (a), exists but condition unmet:** the admit-card print lives on the very page the battery reached (`user/examschedule` → `examList.php`) as an icon-only download button rendered only when `sch_settings.download_admit_card == 1`; staging had it = 0 (SELECT-verified; template id 1 is_active = 1). The print is a browser-print popup (AJAX → HTML → `window.print()`), NEVER a server PDF. No code fix; E6 re-specified (enable the setting, keep template active, click the icon button). Production checklist item (same setting gates production). **Part 3 — Rs 250 parity gap classification (a), vendor by-design:** the Collect Fees screen treats the assessed fine as an informational red "+ 250.00" annotation on the Amount cell, excluded from row/grand-total balances, while the bulk challan is a demand document that includes it via the FL-033 rule; both surfaces agree the fine is exactly Rs 250. No code fix; release-note/training line recommended; optional D-pack parity item carries a double-count risk if the cashier also types the fine in the modal.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane. It corrected two battery readings with evidence: E6 "no admit-card print anywhere" → a settings gate on the page already reached; B3 "screen excludes the fine" → two different quantities sharing the word "fine" (assessed-fine annotation vs collected-fine ledger column).
- **Unusual things:** the print register's stored record content made the EXACT producer HTML recoverable (E3 serials IQRS-2026-000364–367), which is what made the byte-identical 615-page reproduction possible; the resume PDF's leaked `@page { size: … }` printed line on the host was the tell that exposed the HTML_BODY-mode difference; `user/User.php:~1858` holds a plain `WriteHTML($html)` whose consumer is still unidentified — the fix lane is to identify it, read-only.
- **Lesson:** when a PDF renders degenerate but its values are right, bisect the template HEAD, not the content — one CSS declaration in the shared shell can poison every mPDF render at once; and a "missing" UI control may be a settings gate, not a dead path — check `sch_settings` before declaring a feature absent.
- **Promoted to:** FL-122 fix lane (build + deploy to STAGING only, dispatched ~06:40 PKT, agent 96ae43f0, running HEALTHY at the 06:41 census); proof battery (E1/E2/E3 re-run + E5/E7/E8 admit-card legs + one receipt-PDF regression check) held behind the fix; E6 re-run after the `download_admit_card` setting is enabled on staging; D-pack gains the production admit-template + download_admit_card checklist items and the Rs 250 semantics note. FL-122 gates the Wave 3 release's whole server-PDF surface.

## #46 — FL-122 fix lane, `@page size:` strip at the renderUnified seam (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~06:40–06:57 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 96ae43f0, COMPLETE. One-seam patch built, harness-proven, and deployed to STAGING ONLY. Tree proof first (staging Webservice.php 325,925 B vs production 325,577 B); live base fetched byte-exact by base64-pipe (Print_studio.php 18,555 B, md5 `bd644f33…`); patched file 18,948 B, md5 `fa0be8e4…`, backup `Print_studio.php.bak-2026-11-10-fl122`; production marker re-verified untouched at 325,577 B after the deploy. Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/FL-122-FIX.md`.
- **The fix:** `Print_studio::renderUnified()` :153 — the pdf return now strips only the `@page size:` declaration (`preg_replace('~@page\s*\{\s*size:[^;]+;~','@page {',$html)`); preview path byte-identical; no template or vendor-exit changes. Harness (stored register HTML, shipped transform applied verbatim): marksheet **615 pp / 376,271 B → 2 pp**; resume default-mode 514 → 1, HTML_BODY control 1 → 1; receipt fixture never exploded under 4 wrapper geometries and is unchanged after (protected by construction, zero regression).

The lane's harness ran against the stored register HTML rather than a live browser capture, which is what made the 615 → 2 proof exact.
- **Lesson:** one poisoned declaration in a shared producer seam can break every server PDF at once — and one seam fix cures them all; the fix belongs at the seam, not patched template by template.

Of 15 frontend-facing whitelisted methods exactly ONE mutates (`firstrun.dismiss_first_run`); **no whitelisted create/update/submit method exists for any business document.** Both screenshot artefacts proven live-payload rendering defects, NOT fixture leakage: low-stock banner (server returns sentinel `{product:"", below_qty:0}`, app.js renders the strip unconditionally) and "Peak: 1 Orders" (`Math.max(...,1)` floor reused in the label). Minimum write set proposed §6 (W-1…W-11, dependency-ordered) ≈ 2–3 image cycles. Report: `hidden_files/team-write-gap-audit.md`.
- **Mistakes:** none recorded — the audit stayed local and evidence-first, with every finding file-evidenced.
- **Unusual things:** the server side is closer than the frontend: role_matrix.json already grants create/write/submit on the core DocTypes — the gap is frontend write wiring + one save/submit posture decision. Desk can already do full working today and the SPA reads its results live — but that is the engine showing, not the product promise.
- **Lesson:** audit the write path the way users experience it (save → visible result → submitted state), not the way the code claims it — a save that swallows its own rejection and a draft that vanishes from every list is worse than a refused save, because it looks like success.
- **Promoted to:** dated working-ERP roadmap (parent, M1–M3 from this audit + the v2 review); the two screenshot artefacts as S-size fixes; "empty company" as a standing proof case.

## #56 — FL-123 diagnosis lane (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~10:50–10:53 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent c5c3dfdc, COMPLETE (~3 min), read-only throughout — no file or DB row modified, production untouched. Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/FL-123-DIAGNOSIS.md` (19,074 B). **Root cause pinned with source-level proof + byte-faithful local reproduction (75,198 B):** the batch producer (native draft `admin_examresult__printmarksheet_php.php:521`) concatenates 15 COMPLETE HTML documents (renderUnified echo :570–576 + `<pagebreak />` :577–579); mPDF default-mode WriteHTML extracts only to the FIRST `</body>` (vendor Mpdf.php:13324–13325 non-greedy body regex) — documents 2–15 discarded. Controller Examresult.php:251 captures, :267 single WriteHTML. Blast radius: only this exit at ≥2 students; admit/cert producers use the same loop but feed browser exits (proven fine); N=1 immune (why E2/email always passed). The tempting HTML_BODY switch is REJECTED (harness case D: census complete but 15 pp instead of 30 — CSS never loads in that mode). Fix = producer-side merge in the same draft (doc 1 whole + bodies 2..N spliced before its `</body>`). Also closed the register question: the batch print-register records (02:02–02:03 UTC, profile admin_examresult__printmarksheet_php) hold content of 90,273 chars containing ALL 15 students (each admission ×2; first in content order = IQ-STU2139) — the producer HTML is complete, so the fault is DOWNSTREAM in the PDF exit/render/merge step, not selection or controller data.

- **Lesson:** when a batch artefact holds only one item, check the stored producer record before blaming selection — a complete producer record moves the fault downstream to the render/merge step and saves a whole wrong diagnosis.

## #57 — FL-124 diagnosis lane (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~10:50–10:53 PKT)

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 2d3d80dc, COMPLETE (~3 min), read-only throughout — nothing modified on staging or production. Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/FL-124-DIAGNOSIS.md` (9,911 B). **Root cause is NOT a JOIN:** a duplicated accumulator line in the portal view `application/views/user/student/getfees.php:247–248` (`$total_balance_amount = $total_balance_amount + $feetype_balance;` twice back-to-back) doubled EVERY regular-fee row's balance in the footer total at :709 (all 9 fixture rows happen to be Previous Arrears, hence the arrears-specific presentation; transport rows exempt). DB replication of the producer SQL: 1 row per master, no duplication; arithmetic closes exactly (13,750 × 2 = 27,500). Correct producer = admin Fees Statement by name (`reportByName.php:203`, single accumulation).
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane.
- **Unusual things:** the filed symptom ("Previous Arrears double-counted") pointed at the query layer, but the defect was two identical lines in the view — the arrears-specific presentation was a coincidence of the fixture data (all 9 rows are arrears), not a property of the defect.
- **Lesson:** when a total is exactly 2× the truth, suspect the accumulator before the query — replicate the producer SQL first; if it returns one row per master, the doubling lives in the view, not the JOIN.
- **Promoted to:** coordinator-executed one-line fix on staging (line 248 deleted under guard, 247 == 248 verified; backup `getfees.php.bak-2026-11-10-fl124`; 125,276 B md5 `33a0ed62…` → 125,160 B md5 `36a08fb1…`; production's copy byte-identical — defect live there too, fix rides the Wave 3 release) + FL-124 verification battery (browser task f1496ff1).

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 450c367e, COMPLETE (~3 min), build + harness-prove + deploy to STAGING only. Report: `hidden_files/wave3-print/FL-123-FIX.md`. - **Unusual things:** case 3 count note adjudicated NOT a defect — session-scoped bootstrap yields 1,682 UNIQUE students = exact session-21 enrolment; the 1,683rd (id 2080) has no session-21 enrolment; manifest counts the whole table. +3 raw rows = page-overlap re-sends (dedupe by PK per design).
- **Lesson:** a whitelist built from a dump DDL is only as good as that dump — audit every whitelisted column against the LIVE schema (information_schema) before the battery, not after it fails; and a battery lane's own script bug must be fixed script-side and re-run, never patched into the server to make the numbers pass.

- **Lesson:** in a multi-lane office, read-only verification and staging writes must not share a window — supervisors declare write windows, or inspectors re-baseline at inspection start and treat mid-window drift as a sequencing finding, not a team error. (Inspector A's own conduct is the model: it named the drift, proved its source, and kept its verdicts claim-by-claim.)

Its substantive report (findings, md5s, held items) and its deliverable file never arrived; batch3-3b/ is empty on disk.

- **Lesson:** a parity harness must consume production-shaped inputs or the parity proves a fiction; and a correction is only useful if the thing it corrects is on file. Lanes: file first, report second, amend third — in that order.

- **Lesson:** an inspector that sets production-gate preconditions must name them as numbered gates, not prose — numbered gates are what the CEO can dispatch against, and (1) + (3) were closed by the very next lane (#186).

## #203 — FL-080 R3 picker diagnosis lane (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~15:47–16:14 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** Agent b4698819, DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE, build NOT executed — transport outage. Diagnosis (live staging reads, DB asserted `u238632175_test123`): the Search Due Fees picker is fsg-level (`Studentfee::feesearch()` → `Feesessiongroup_model::getFeesByGroup()`, filters = session 21 + `nature != 'custom'` only, no archive exclusion). "Previous Arrears" ×200 is MECHANISM, not a defect — group 2034 holds 200 fsg (one per amount variant), every other group exactly 1 (200 + 951 archived + 12 = 1,163 fsg ✓). The real defect is cosmetic: the 951 `ZZ-ARCHIVED-%` groups still list because the apply renamed `fee_groups.name` only and nothing excludes them. Archived selections are noise, not wrong money — the due-fees search is driven from `student_fees_master` and 0 masters point at any archived group (inspector-proven). Side-finding: R3's "picker = 1" expectation was written against the fee_groups-level census; the UI picker is fsg-level — the spec conflated two levels. Fix specified exactly: one clause `$this->db->not_like('fee_groups.name', 'ZZ-ARCHIVED-', 'after');` in `getFeesByGroup()` (callers audited — all selection lists), with full execution checklist in WAVE4-EXECUTION.md. CEO re-dispatched the build as its own lane the same hour.
- **Mistakes:** none by the lane — it captured the live code + census during the one successful SSH probe in the window and left a complete, executable checklist instead of a dead end.
- **Unusual things:** for ~55 min the VM egress proxy refused every SSH CONNECT (13+ attempts), the VPS hop failed identically, and staging HTTPS stalled (HTTP 000 at ~10.5 s) while production HTTPS stayed healthy (200 in 1.8 s) — a gateway outage, not a host outage; one mid-window probe succeeded, which is how the evidence was captured.
- **Lesson:** when transport dies mid-lane, convert the remaining work into a numbered, ready-to-run checklist inside the record — the resume lane then starts at the patch, not at the diagnosis.

## #216 — Simple-signup deploy lane (Operqon, 2026-11-10 ~17:11–18:23 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** COMPLETE as a lane, DEPLOY NOT LIVE. Steps 1–4 done with evidence (pre-flight BOARD GREEN 16/16; theme overlay + MANIFEST regen 497 entries, sha-verified; final docker gate 591 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed; Keycloak KC-01…KC-10 all PUTs 204, read-back 15/15 PASS incl. both per-action verify-email lifespans "86400" on KC 26.8.1, theme bundles sha-verified, both realms' well-known 200). Step 5: FOUR attempts, four auto-rollbacks. Attempt 4's outcome was UNVERIFIED when the lane closed (egress proxy failure spell blocked its verification calls); the 18:26 Inspector probe verified DEPLOY_EXIT=1 on-box and a MIXED live state (see below). Final report `team-simple-signup-deploy.md` was NOT written; the progress file is checkpointed through attempt 3 + attempt-4 launch.
- **Mistakes (one per attempt, each root-caused in-lane):** (1) runner exported 3 of the 4 env vars the compose file hard-requires (missing OPERQON_FRAPPE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID) — fixed by sourcing it on-box from the running container. (2) The shipped script's `docker compose build api` is a silent no-op (the image is built only by the `migrate` service) so the old 2026-11-08 image ran and plans 404'd — fixed by pre-building from the staged tree and tagging r3-customer (old preserved as r3-customer-pre-ss). (3) Acceptance expects POST /api/v1/public/plans → 405, but the shipped Caddy route is GET-only so the edge returned 404 — fixed by manual-review route change to GET POST + path-scoped CSP. (4) After plans PASS 3 the script exited rc=1; the immediately preceding log output shows TWO connect-src lines where deploy-note (b) requires ONLY the plans URL on public pages — the CSP acceptance is the prime suspect (not proven by a named check line).
- **Unusual things:** the trap's "ROLLBACK COMPLETE" restores $ROOT + apex files but NEVER re-tags the image — after attempt 4 the running r2-api container is still the NEW image da553ade (tag r3-customer → da553ade) and GET /api/v1/public/plans returns 200 with the real plan list, while the marker is untouched and $ROOT was restored. The provider is therefore in a MIXED state (new API live, old files, old marker), not the clean rollback the trap claims. Also: the lane's own verification was killed by 27+ consecutive egress CONNECT failures, and its closing turn hit a safety refusal on tool calls — it reported honestly instead of guessing.
- **Lesson:** a deploy script's "ROLLBACK COMPLETE" must be verified against the RUNNING IMAGE, not just restored files — re-tag + recreate + old-behaviour probe belong inside the trap, not in a lane's manual follow-up. And an acceptance check whose expected shape lives only in a deploy note (CSP note (b)) will fail opaquely — pin the exact expected header in the script with the check name in the log.
- **CORRECTION (coordinator, ~18:30 PKT — read before acting on the "prime suspect" above):** the "TWO connect-src lines" premise is REFUTED by live probe: request-access.html returns exactly ONE connect-src, plans-only (correct); /customer/ returns the broad policy (correct). The failing check after PASS 3 in attempt 4 is therefore UNIDENTIFIED, not the CSP acceptance — the completion lane's first task is to name it from the full ss4 log + acceptance script. CEO decision already taken: complete the deploy (attempt 5), do not roll back the image.

Defect D-1.1-A found+fixed in-lane: legacy `h1,h2{color:#555}` (usertemplate style.css) overrode token colours — pin surface headings explicitly in every later Phase 1 surface. **Open 1 CLOSED** — tokens CSS + proto login served byte-equal to local/on-host. Residual (named, accepted shape): the 11 screenshots are mirror renders of the actual live-served HTML + md5-verified staging assets (headless Chrome on this VM cannot use the egress proxy); the formal live-capture leg is one short browser-task pass with the saved Super Admin login if ever wanted.
- **Mistakes:** two of the lane's own early retry loops fed `payload.txt` itself to a remote `bash -s`, so the remote shell tried to execute the base64 payload as a script (harmless, caught by md5 gates, no writes). Host awk treats an un-triggered redirect target as nonexistent — the first split segment silently decoded empty (md5 `d41d8cd9…`), caught by the pre-state gates and fixed by direct re-upload of the md5-verified view segment before any proof ran.
- **Unusual things:** the SSH gateway was in a ~50-minute CONNECT-refusal stretch mid-lane; retries with sleeps remained the route. Mid-lane the owner reported staging rendering unstyled — the 750-directory static-asset fault (Phase 0 tar-pipe carried the VM's 750 dir modes); the parent fixed it on-host (chmod 755) and the lane re-proved with a complete post-fix re-fetch (24 assets, every md5 identical to on-host) and appended a §8 addendum correcting the Open-1 closure wording — the afternoon's 0-byte responses were the directory-mode fault, not just egress.
- **Lesson:** the payload rides ssh's command channel on stdin (`rssh-retry.sh "$(cat deploy-remote.sh)" < payload.txt`) — never feed a payload file to `bash -s`; pre-create split targets before awk redirects, or the first segment decodes empty. And a deploy lane must assert directory modes (755) + served-bytes on its own assets, not just file md5s — the 750-dir trap is now a standing check after every deploy.

- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 43259214, COMPLETE — **DEPLOY LIVE, READY FOR PILOT3.** Attempt 5: **DEPLOY_EXIT=0**. Root cause #4 identified first (see below), one-line fix, MANIFEST regen (497 entries, identical manifest sha `61ac643a…` on-box and in the local composed tree, sha256sum -c 100% clean). In-image gate **591 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed**; **PUBLIC PLANS ACCEPTANCE: PASS** (PASS 3 + PORTAL IDENTITY FLAGS: PASS). Step-6 smoke ALL PASS (independent probes ~18:52–18:56 PKT): plans 200, intake GET/POST 404, POST plans 405, verify/complete-signup pages 200, served-bytes 10/10 MATCH, Rektrs + demo2 pong 200. Live state now CONSISTENT — new API image da553ade… + new apex files + new well-known (stage "simple-signup", `public_plans_path`) + new Caddyfile (plans route GET POST, path-scoped CSP); Keycloak Step 4 live; PV-06 still NOT provisioned (resend inert-503 by design, KC-native resend is the path). Marker untouched (`6bd1cbe1…` — moves LAST, after pilot3 publishes + battery evidence). Rollback point `/root/operqon-simple-signup.20261110134031`; old image preserved as `r3-customer-pre-ss`. Final report `hidden_files/team-simple-signup-deploy.md` written (the first lane never wrote it); progress file all 7 steps checked. No pilot3 records created; no Rektrs/demo2 data touched.
- **Mistakes:** (1) The attempt-4 failure was first blamed on a "two connect-src lines" theory (debrief #216) — REFUTED by live probe (exactly one connect-src, plans-only); the theory cost a cycle. The lane instead ran the acceptance with `bash -x` against live state and the xtrace named the failing check in one run: line 44 `[ "$(code "$CONTROL/tenants.html")" = 200 ]` — the console returns **301** (unauthenticated requests redirect to /?) while `code()` is a plain curl with no `-L`; followed, it returns 200. The defect was in the acceptance script (a bare-200 assertion predating the console's clean-URL/auth-redirect behaviour), NOT the product. (2) A worker summary conflated SSH retry-loop output ("attempt $i failed") with deploy-attempt evidence — attempt outcomes verify only from the done file + deploy log. (3) Two probe artefacts in-lane: `/api/pong` is not the pong endpoint (real one is `/api/method/ping`); the first dashboard.html probe forgot `-L` and hashed the empty 301 body — a wrong probe looks exactly like a product failure.
- **Unusual things:** the trap's rollback (attempt 4) restored files but never re-tagged the image, so the NEW image was already live when this lane started — which is exactly why the CEO decision was "complete the deploy, do not roll back". The line-44 fix and the attempt-3/4 Caddy deviations (GET POST route + path-scoped CSP) are documented deviations, NOT yet folded into the canonical tree — the next composition must fold them in. The shell comment's literal `frappe.csrf_token = "..."` text remains a scraper hazard, named as a future-cycle follow-up.
- **Lesson:** a silent `set -e` acceptance failure hides the failing check — always re-run the acceptance with `bash -x` against live state before theorising. Probe endpoints must be the real ones (`/api/method/ping`, `-L` on clean-URL pages). Retry-loop output is not deploy-attempt evidence.

Household_service v5 (finance section) + admin Household module v4 on STAGING only: pay-once-allocate with FIFO (one receipt `FAM-<date>-<id>`, per-line journal, R-5 overpayment refusal inside the transaction), combined + per-child household statements (Wave 3 print layer, A4-P), CF re-pointed to the household spine (family resolution, collect/preview/reverse — CF payment tables untouched by the re-pointed surface), wallet retired in-controller per D-F2, 4 CF accounts archived (rows frozen, never deleted). One named OPEN leg: office statement-format sign-off (built to spec D-F4, office signs off later). Production untouched.
- **Mistakes:** four implementation defects caught by the battery and fixed in-lane: (1) CF builder-state corruption — the spine helper used CI's query builder inside `getFamilyStudents`' own build, merging the queries ("Column 'id' in SELECT is ambiguous", 0-byte dues/statement responses) — fixed with raw queries; (2) service construction — CF helper passed the DB object where the constructor requires `array('db' => …)`, plus one wrong preview key (`total_paisa` → `allocated_paisa`); (3) fine-encoding defect — CF's `amount_fine` = fine-take leaves the collected fine still owed under the governed view's arithmetic (view adds Σ(amount_fine) to what is owed) — fixed to `amount = base + fine`, `amount_fine = 0.00`, split preserved in the journal; (4) JSON-object encoding — deposit `amount_detail` was emitted as JSON lists instead of inv_no-keyed objects at three sites (would have corrupted reversal) — fixed with `(object)` casts, byte-exact restoration proven. Plus a journaling slip: the archive UPDATE committed but its journal insert used a wrong column (`batch` for `batch_id`) and was lost — the row was completed at close from captured before/after state with the reason disclosed. Two fixture-build aborts (column slips) left partial spine rows — recovered by name pattern and deleted in full, population back to baseline before the successful build.

Scope limits named in the record: transport dues excluded from household allocation v1 (outside the governed view); household receipts have no PDF exit in this slice; CF dues *display* still uses CF's own computation over the spine-resolved child set — only collection/preview/reversal moved to the governed service.
- **Lesson:** when re-pointing a legacy surface onto a governed position, prove the encoding against the governed view's own arithmetic (`SHOW CREATE VIEW`) before trusting the legacy encoding — the legacy fine-as-take and the vendor's remaining-fine rule measure different quantities, and the mismatch only shows as a residue on a full-payment leg. And never let a query-builder helper run inside another query's build — spine resolution gets raw queries.

- **Mistakes:** none by the battery — it retried ~8 min before failing (correct behaviour) and its report correctly separated "login submit 500s" from a credential failure.
- **Unusual things:** the 500 was invisible to the battery's own view (it only ever saw the login page fail) — the split between "login succeeded, landing failed" needed the host-side CI log, which the lane could not read.
- **Lesson:** a deploy that lands a view before its library load breaks every signed-in session's landing page — load path first, view second, and prove the dashboard renders in a real session before calling a deploy done. A login-500 must be split by log evidence (login success vs landing failure) before anyone blames credentials.

Department launchpad built on staging (FL-094 shell + FL-099 counts): bento cards, Today strip, honest labels; gate legs (b)–(f) PASS incl. §4.4 Dashboard 30/30 pairs; gate (a) PARTIAL — Teacher role rendered + reconciled same-window; the Super Admin render legs were NOT RUN (blocked by the lane's own defect below + an egress-auth episode) and remain owed as a closeout. Root cause: CI3 view semantics — views execute in the `CI_Loader` context, so the view's `$this->load->library('calmcampus_launchpad')` silently never registered the property and line 9's `snapshot()` hit null for every role (19 log lines, all inside the window). The CEO's initial diagnosis (deploy ordering) was corrected by the lane on evidence: library, controller and view were all deployed and present. Fix: dashboard.php loads via `get_instance()` (final md5 `a28b1031…`, flawed build preserved as `.bak-2026-11-10-dash14-fix`); Admin.php deliberately untouched. - **Unusual things:** the lane's first authenticated render came at 21:27 — after real sessions had already hit the defect — because an egress-auth episode delayed its own proof; its sequencing failure is owned in the record. The Launchpad controller path was never affected (controller-context load), so worklists rendered fine throughout while the dashboard died.
- **Lesson (now a standing rule in the record for all remaining Phase 1 items):** deploy library → controller → view → CSS, then IMMEDIATELY prove one authenticated render and tail the CI log before proceeding — a view deploy without a render proof is not a completed deploy, and no other lane's battery should ever be a surface's first render. CI3-specific: never load a library from inside a view via `$this->load` — it silently no-ops in the loader context; use `get_instance()`.

## Debrief #260 — Rams provisioning recovery RESUME lane (Operqon, 2026-11-10 ~22:33 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 4cb1d753, COMPLETE — stopped at its fence with a precise blocker, as instructed. Root cause PINNED: `bench new-site rams-al-kayan-trading-company.stage.operqon.cloud --install-app erpnext` exited non-zero ~16:01 UTC after writing the skeleton + site_config.json; the helper discards subprocess output (DEVNULL), so the frappe-level error text is UNRECOVERABLE — itself a hardening finding that G-1 already fixes for future jobs. Two verified blockers: (1) a plain executor re-run fails instantly ("Site already exists but is not an R2-owned site" — no ownership marker at /var/lib/operqon-r2-provisioner/<site>.json, so idempotent resume cannot adopt the partial shell); the empty shell must be bench-dropped first, and the executor's drop lives only inside its rollback flow (requires state completed). (2) No deployed API edge returns a failed job to claimable, and no edge exits tenant `suspended` — the state is "manual reconciliation" by construction. Minimal reconciliation proposed (bench-drop shell + one-time requeue of the SAME job failed→queued + tenant suspended→provisioning, then the unmodified executor path, all audited) — NOT executed; it crosses the lane's fences. Options 1 (reconcile tonight) vs 2 (durable fix in the Console MVP release, Rams as first proof) put to Assad with the coordinator's recommendation (1 now + 2 in the release). Evidence `hidden_files/rams-provisioning-recovery.md` (14.5 KB). No writes made by the lane; Rektrs/demo2 untouched, marker unchanged 6bd1cbe1….
- **Mistakes:** none in-lane.
- **Unusual things:** egress went BLOCKED-EGRESS from 22:26 (7 consecutive CONNECT refusals), so the on-box md5 identity + site-DB census could not run; the mechanics rest on the release-simple-signup tree of record (field-for-field match to box state) and the report says so. Contrast with lane 1, which died on the same gateway without writing its report — the resume lane's mandatory incremental checkpointing is what made this delivery survive.
- **Lesson:** a recovery lane must write its evidence file incrementally from preflight, not at the end — the gateway kills lanes, not files. And: any helper that discards subprocess output makes its own failures undiagnosable — capture the output (G-1 now does exactly this for provisioning).

## Debrief #261 — Desktop M5 engine-legs proof lane (IQRS, 2026-11-10 ~22:53 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** Agent 002b4bcd, COMPLETE. Verdict: legs 1, 2 and 4 PASS; leg 3 data side PASS, shell path FAIL — the M5 engine-legs gate is NOT fully green. The shell failure is **D5L-1** (new defect, this lane's finding): `HomeworkCommsProjector` syllabus phase is not re-runnable (subjectLocal via getGeneratedKeys on an upsert; fallback returns -1 → FK throw at syllabus_lesson insert on the 2nd projection). Amplification found while verifying: `projectAll` wraps all projectors in ONE transaction, so the throw rolls back everything — until D5L-1 is fixed, a profile's typed tables freeze at their first-projection state and every shell sync ends "offline refresh failed". Fix shape recorded (SELECT after upsert / RETURNING; never let -1 reach an insert). The D5L-1 fix + M6 live-drill resume lane was dispatched immediately after (~22:54 PKT) with the fix as step 0.
- **D6-1 fixed in-lane (M6 lane's finding, this lane's projector):** `AttendanceProjector.java:224` now reads `is_active` from the STUDENT row instead of the enrolment row. Reconciliation exact vs server ground truth: roster 1,682 = **1,669 active / 13 inactive** (before: 0 active); class day-status rows with roster_count > 0: 0 → 3. Build OK, snapshot gate GREEN, no schema change. The AFTER numbers were produced by `AttendanceProjector.project()` run directly — `projectAll` would have rolled them back with the D5L-1 throw. Student 2080 is enrolment-less (invisible to desktop sync by data fact).
- **Mistakes:** none in-lane on the verdict itself — the lane proved the defect rather than working around it, and filed D5L-1 with the exact fix shape instead of patching the projector inline.
- **Unusual things:** (1) a concurrent lane's `./build.sh` (`rm -rf build/classes`) killed the legs run mid-flight with `NoClassDefFoundError SyncFacade$SyncReport` — root-caused from class-file timestamps, not a code failure; private classes dir made the remaining runs immune. (2) First harness launch died silently mid-bootstrap — box memory exhausted under three concurrent lanes; capped `-Xmx1g` thereafter. (3) After a runtime restart the snapshot gate failed with `no glassgtk3` — replacement VM image lacks libxtst6; `apt-get install -y libxtst6` restored it (same class of repair as the PHP-CLI reinstall precedent in AGENTS.md). (4) Egress gateway dropped SSH CONNECT tunnels and Staffpull manifest handshakes intermittently through the evening; retries succeed.
- **Lesson:** projector proofs must reconcile SEMANTIC splits (active/inactive, status distributions), not row totals — row counts masked D6-1 completely. And: re-runnability of every projector phase is a gate, not a nicety — one non-re-runnable phase inside a single-transaction `projectAll` freezes the whole typed layer. Lanes sharing one `./build.sh` must use private class dirs.

## Debrief #262 — Console MVP G-0 (owner single-login) completion lane (Operqon, 2026-11-10 ~23:16 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** Agent ae77e7cf, COMPLETE. Finished the owner single-login build in `~/workspace/operqon-team/scratch-owner-access` (copy of release-p1) and filed `hidden_files/team-owner-access-build.md`. Core from lane 1 (OWNER_ROLE, permits() superset, exactly-one-role rule intact, SoD waiver, owner_unification_meta via the audit() wrapper) plus FOUR workflows the wrapper did not reach, each fixed with the same minimal pattern: deal desk (module-local `_require` gave owner a 500, local `_no_self`, local audit() bypassing the marker), dunning (service-level `created_by == actor` 409 in publish/reject — waived via `owner_unified` param), support sessions (string role gate `!= "operqon:operator"` refused owner with 403), settlement offline-approve (service-level actor-string SoD in `settle_invoice` — waived via `settle_as_owner`, then `_stamp_owner_settlement` re-stamps the settlement events and re-signs the HMAC audit chain so verify_chain still passes). Console verdict CHANGED + FIXED: `app.mjs` role-gated visibility would have hidden almost every panel from an owner session — owner gate added (+215 B, file 65,873 B, under the 66,000 B cap). New tests 10/10 pass; full suite 819 passed / 3 skipped / 1 failed vs baseline 810/3/0 — the single failure is the stale 8-role census assertion (`test_eng190_negative_suite.py:754`, `ALL_ROLES` local constant), deliberately NOT edited in-lane; the one-line merge fix (`| {OWNER_ROLE}`) rides composition, expected suite 820/3/0. No deploy; provider marker untouched; `payment_policy.py` verified byte-identical to release-p1.
- **Mistakes:** none in-lane.
- **Unusual things:** (1) An owner-only "supersede" block in `request_provision` was prototyped during test diagnosis and REVERTED — it changed state-machine behaviour beyond the permits/SoD/marker pattern; consequence by design: an operator provisioning request (owner included) still meets the existing open-job 409 fence when a trial-automation job already exists. (2) The app.mjs budget cap bit mid-lane: first cut landed at 66,125 B and failed 8 frontend budget tests; compressing one comment to a single line landed at 65,873 B — only ~127 B headroom left, any further app.mjs addition in this release must respect it or re-ratify the cap. (3) The settlement re-stamp is the only place in the build that rewrites audit rows after the fact — it re-signs the chain from the event before the tail, and the test proves verify_chain passes.
- **Lesson:** a wrapper-based audit marker only covers paths that use the wrapper — modules with a local audit(), a service-level SoD, or a string role gate silently exclude the owner even when the core is correct; owner coverage must be audited workflow by workflow, not assumed from the core. And: a census assertion that a correct implementation must fail is a merge step, not a lane defect — leave it unedited, name the exact line, and let composition carry it.

## Debrief #267 — printDiv C-J §5.3 diagnosis + remedy lane (IQRS, 2026-11-11 ~00:19–00:27 PKT)

Remedy (fixture only, journal-led, reversible): paid the balance in full through the app's own `Household_service` v6.1 `allocateHouseholdPayment` — one transaction, R-5 enforced; preview confirmed household dues of exactly 1,335,000 paisa with remaining-after 0, and a membership guard asserted household 1413 contains ONLY student 3699 before any write. - **Lesson:** a systemic "every route redirects" symptom is a guard rule, not a broken page — read the controller constructor first. And: paying a fixture's balance through the app's own service (with preview + membership guard + journal) is the reversible remedy; hand-editing fee tables would have left the position unreconcilable.

Non-session battery: 9/9 new production exits → HTTP 307 to `site/userlogin` (session guard fires, no 404/500). Rollback armed, unexecuted. Recorded as §9 of PRINTDIV-CJ-EXECUTION.md.
- **Mistakes:** none in-lane — the first verify run's 42 "mismatches" were a `$10` positional-parameter bug in the verify script itself (every "got" value equalled the true expected md5); the lane fixed the script to array indexing and re-ran clean instead of trusting the output.
- **Unusual things:** (1) the egress gateway was in a long dead window ("proxy closed during CONNECT") — first driver aborted after 9/12 chunks (production untouched, abort precedes any host write outside `~/`), second driver SIGTERM'd mid-upload; before resuming, a read-only state probe proved production still pristine AND all 12 chunks had in fact landed at full size, so the finish run used per-chunk truncate-write + size verification with no append pass. ## Debrief #286 — Rams setup_masters fix + mvp6 + cap 4→5 + Rams attempt-5 lane (Operqon, 2026-11-11 ~12:20–13:14 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** Agent d1a594e1, COMPLETE. **Step 0 C6 completed:** both mvp5 push cards had in fact landed in the mvp5 lane's final seconds (C6a `2cedc964…`, handover C6 `5928fe6d…`) — only its report text was stale; marker moved C5 → C6 VERIFIED. **Diagnosis exact:** the only code defect was observability — `bench_setup_masters` (and `bench_tenant_company`/`bench_sso`/`bench_support_provision`) discarded bench stderr/stdout on failure, so attempt 4's exception text existed nowhere. Attempt 4 died of the same throw. **Lane STOPPED per brief + owner Option 2:** no further cap change (cap now exhausted at 5), no manual reconciliation, no queue surgery. Rams suspended, attempts 5, manual_required; subscription byte-identical; Rektrs + demo2 untouched. Report: `hidden_files/team-rams-setup-masters-fix.md`. Worker spot-check this run: mvp6 MANIFEST sha `fab7b3b5…`, 577 entries — matches the report.
- **Mistakes:** (1) the first C7a staging attempt used an unscoped `rsync --delete` against the clone root (the clone is the full repo; the release tree is an overlay) — produced a local-only commit that was never pushed; the clone was reset to C6 and the overlay redone scoped, pushed history clean. (2) Root-owned logs seen in the first clone probe were a `docker cp` artefact of the lane's own copy pipeline — refuted against the live directory before it became a finding.
- **Unusual things:** (1) the one input the clone programme could NOT replicate was the staging bench's redis-QUEUE content (diag queues start empty) — and that omission turned out to be exactly where the true cause lived; five faithful reproductions all passed while the live bench failed. (2) Both mvp5 push cards landed seconds after that lane's final write while its report said pending — report staleness vs ground truth, caught by the successor's step-0 triple check.
- **Lesson:** a reproduction bench must replicate the live system's load/queue state, not just its data — a byte-identical shell passes while the live bench fails on queue backlog. And captured stderr is what turned a fifth failure into a diagnosis instead of another blind cycle. - **Lanes + outcome:** Agents b39de9b6 + resume lane, COMPLETE. **RAMS AL KAYAN IS LIVE — the third real tenant published.** Owner's queue decision executed: one persistent RQ worker added to the staging bench compose (oc23, queues default,long,short, restart unless-stopped; backup `compose.yaml.pre-rqworker-20261111`; `up -d --no-deps worker`, nothing else touched). **Drain proven:** default 1,312 → 822 → 711 → 635 → 518 → 22 → **0 at 09:49:30 UTC**, sustained; long 25 → 0. Failed registry at drain completion 754/7/13 (774 of 1,337 failed — sampled = stale-job noise: IncorrectSitePath for dead sites, MySQL 1045 for deleted DBs). **Cap 5→6** via the governed env route (backup `/root/merchant.env.pre-cap6-20261111`; readyz 200/200; env settings carry no audit event — known gap). Diagnosis 09:51:34 UTC (audit 1120). **Attempt 6 (resume lane):** guarded pair (guard row exactly failed|5|empty-key; fresh key `eecd3d4f-…`; provisioner 200 requested → approver 200 queued, SoD intact) → daemon claim 10:32:09 UTC → **all steps passed in 41 s**: site created, SSO, support, **setup_masters SEEDED (UOM 239, Customer Group 5, Item Group 6, Supplier Group 8, Territory 3, Price List 2, FY 1)**, company configured, **auto-published 10:32:49 UTC (audit 1122–1130)**. Job published|6; tenant active; subscription byte-identical; Rektrs + demo2 active/untouched; smoke 5/5 incl. audit chain verifies; worker running, queues 0, timer active. Report: `hidden_files/team-rams-attempt6-rq-worker.md`.
- **Mistakes:** (1) the prior lane launched the pair once with `/usr/bin/python3`, which lacks Playwright — `ModuleNotFoundError`, died instantly, zero effect (verified no partial retry; Rams state untouched). The resume lane proved the interpreter first (`/root/smoke-venv/bin/python3 -c "import playwright"`) and launched under it. (2) The prior lane's prepared `/tmp/pair_launch2.sh` did not survive on-box — /tmp is not durable across a long spell; the resume lane rewrote the launch (guarded, systemd-detached) from its own brief.
- **Unusual things:** (1) the ~2h+ egress spell (`proxy closed during CONNECT` from ~09:55 UTC) outlasted the first lane entirely — the pair, a ~1-minute job, was the only step that needed a live window; it fired inside the first window the resume lane caught (10:31 UTC) and completed on-box under systemd while the monitor was still blind for three more rounds. (2) The failed registry GREW after the drain (999 at 10:31, 1,000 at 10:37) — the worker keeps failing newly enqueued stale items from live-site traffic; queued depth stayed 0, which is the number that matters. (3) One unrelated audit event (1121 `dunning_run_completed`) landed between the diagnosis baseline (1120) and the pair — baselines must be read as "no events FOR THIS JOB", not "no events". (4) SPA-lane fencing held both ways: pairing stayed oc23 through the attempt (SPA gate still running), and the SPA lane's recreate set preserves the worker service.
- **Lesson:** the pair runs under the smoke-venv interpreter, never /usr/bin/python3 — prove `import playwright` before every launch. And for egress spells: make the launch itself idempotent (state-guarded, detached on-box), so a blind monitor never tempts a re-fire — verify state on-box, never infer it from the launch side. Six attempts, five distinct layers (bench new-site → grants → resume gap → install hook → discarded stderr → workerless queue), each fixed in product/infrastructure and proven before the next attempt burned: the Rams chain is now the programme's reference recovery.

## Debrief #291 — SPA repackage + pairing oc24 lane (Operqon, 2026-11-11 ~14:43–16:05 PKT)
- **Lane + outcome:** SPA repackage lane, STOPPED at step 3 per its hard constraint after completing steps 1–2. **Repackage DONE:** canonical's hand-carried bundle v-9693b59c694f was stale exactly as briefed (no CSRF helper/marker/guard, no GAP-12–15 endpoint keys, 121-line pre-CSRF config). Route = the documented packaging snapshot (GAPS.md: committed source keeps fixture defaults, the snapshot flips them): built `oc24-snapshot/` (frontend + pack pair), flipped exactly 4 config lines (sales/buying/admin/pos → live, mirroring the oc21 shipped truth), updated the snapshot harness §6a0 pin, harness PASS standalone, snapshot inputs byte-identical to the oc21 snapshot's → `package_frontend.py` minted **v-2efe04cb5215** (21 assets, --check OK) — the same content address oc23 serves, now freshly generated into canonical with a full census (all 7 switches + auth live, CSRF ×2 + guard-before-marker, all 10 GAP-12–15 keys verbatim, packaged tree + shell byte-identical to oc21line's). **Re-verify DONE:** verify_image pin updated in place v-9693→v-2efe (the per-cycle edit, oc21 precedent); suites per-suite green at exact canonical counts (saas 139 · packs 80 · integrations 137); role-matrix accounting UNCHANGED 272 rows / 45 DocTypes. Combined-process 8-failure + scripts/tests 11-failure sets proven byte-identical on the pristine pre-lane tree (pre-existing). **Build BLOCKED:** on-box `docker build` (context staged /root/oc24-build/snapshot) passed every verify_image section to the LAST one, then died: `AssertionError: oc22 DocType missing in image: operqon_country_profile`. Root cause = a defect IN verify_image.py line 335 (oc22 section): it asserts the 12 oc22 DocTypes at `apps/operqon_core/operqon_core/doctype/…` — one level short; Frappe layout puts them under the namesake module folder (`…/operqon_core/operqon_core/doctype/…`), the triple form the same file's oc14 outbox assertion (line 204) uses correctly. Proven by three isolated on-box experiments (context census complete; plain-COPY ditest all 36 doctypes in-image; real-Dockerfile-shape ditest: asserted path absent, find locates the file at the triple path). The defect was masked since the oc22 section was added because every canonical build died earlier at the stale-frontend pin — the repackage unmasked it. Per the brief's stop rule the lane did NOT edit the assertion; the exact one-line fix is written in the report for the coordinator to sanction. Gate + swap never ran; the staging bench was never touched (timer found ACTIVE, no pause taken; the attempt-6 lane's new worker service found live and preserved by non-interference; bench still oc23, cap still 5, $ROOT/marker untouched). Report: `hidden_files/team-spa-repackage-oc24.md`.
- **Mistakes:** (1) First ditest used `docker build -q`, which swallowed the RUN output the test existed to capture — reran as a container inspection. (2) A `pgrep -f "docker build"` probe self-matched its own ssh command line and briefly reported a phantom running build; only the build-log check is trustworthy for launch state — cost one verification cycle. (3) Early path analysis repeatedly miscounted the operqon_core nesting from memory before settling it with an explicit tree print.
- **Unusual things:** (1) The "stale bundle" and the gate defect were stacked in the same file: fixing the bundle id exposed that the gate had never once validated the oc22 DocTypes it claims to guard — the oc22 content has been "gate-proven" by a section that could never pass. (2) The repackage provably reproduces the exact bundle already live (v-2efe04cb5215): content addressing turned "is the new bundle real?" into a byte-equality proof instead of a judgement call. (3) Egress was down in long spells (~50 min of failed CONNECTs); every detached/on-box artefact (build log, staged context, gate script) survived the outage by design.
- **Lesson:** a gate section that has never passed is not a gate — when a build has always died before section N, treat sections after the historical death point as UNVERIFIED code, and expect the first clean run to find their bugs. And in Frappe path assertions, count the module folder: apps/<app>/<package>/<module-folder>/doctype — the namesake module level is the one everyone drops.
