### Debrief #414 — BL-142: cluster-B gates + per-form CSRF + the 3750 hygiene rider (2026-11-12)

- **Outcome:** COMPLETE on staging. 14 files: NEW `Pk_csrf` per-scope token helper (not consumed on success — preserves BL-031's retry flow); gates on admin/Offlinepayment (reads can_view / update can_edit), the portal Offlinepayment IDOR (ownership scope + 404), Examresult (8 read doors can_view, updaterank can_edit, generatemarksheet can_add); tokens on counter collect (both doors), household save/reverse, pkfees reverse, offline update, both Examresult writes; Pkstudents profile default 3750→governed first record. Batteries: repro proved the defects live; v3+v4 closed every cluster — deny (303 POST / 307 GET → admin/unauthorized, all 14 doors), IDOR 4/4, CSRF refuse/accept set complete, approve posts exactly one deposit ×2, hygiene 4/4. Guards held: exam-19 fingerprint exact in every run, ranks never generated, Print md5s untouched, BL-141 seams green, production read-backs == preflight, census 122/122.
- **Mistakes (mine, all caught by my own evidence):** (1) A REAL bug shipped in MY code: `first_student_id()` passed `$this->session_id()` as a `where()` argument — CI3's query builder is stateful, so the inner `get()` corrupted the half-built chain and the no-id profile 500'd. Lesson: never call a builder-touching method mid-chain; resolve scalars first. The battery caught what local lint could not. (2) I put a stateful money battery inside an 8× retry loop — run 1 shredded the staged passwords, so later runs were inert, but the DESIGN was wrong: retries belong on transport, never on state-changing batteries. A1's arithmetic audit (189000→174000 across three runs) proved the money fired exactly once; it was luck-shaped discipline, not design. (3) A close-out runner gated on battery COMPLETION, not PASS — it deleted fixtures while legs were still red; re-minted and re-closed properly. Gate close-outs on the PASS string. (4) Four battery iterations were spent re-learning shapes I should have captured once early: the vendor deny is a 303/307 + Location with a 0-byte body (nothing to grep), household allocation lands on the A2 master, tokens land JSON-escaped in other pages' markup, and the profile view prints neither admission_no nor the raw stored name — capture REAL response shapes before writing assertions, not after three red runs.
- **Lesson for the fleet:** the deny/assertion contract for this vendor stack is now written down (BL-142 record §5/§8): first-response status + Location, body assertions only where a body exists. And a token helper decision worth reusing: per-scope, session-stored, hash_equals, NOT consumed on success when the underlying door has its own idempotency registry — consuming would break the legitimate retry the registry exists to allow.

## Debrief #421 — DEMO-SEED lane: D-040/D-045 staging demo dataset (2026-11-12 ~19:00–19:35 PKT)

- **Outcome:** COMPLETE on staging. 30 DEMO students (3758–3787, IQ-STU3314–3343) in cs3 + DEMO exam group 29 / exam 22 (published) with 6 schedule subjects, 30 enrolments, 180 marks — bands below 8 / pass 14 / high 8, so the PF-2 Risk Matrix flipped from honest-empty to REAL on the live dashboard ("DEMO Assessment Group", 8 below the pass line). Timetables 108 rows (3 class-sections × Mon–Sat × 6). Staff attendance 1,130 rows (113 teachers × 10 working days). Demo-student register 210 rows (heatmap populated: Four–Daffodils 90/90/80…%). Holidays 8 (annual_calendar 7–14). Events 3. Exam-19 fingerprint identical; demo students hold 0 fee masters; production read-back clean (0 demo rows); census restored 122/122, proof admin 203 deleted, creds refused, password shredded. Record `phase4/DEMO-SEED-EXECUTION.md`, inventory `phase4/demo-seed-inventory.csv`, evidence `phase4/evidence-seed/`.
- **Mistakes:** (1) First enrolment attempt grepped the candidate page as HTML — the endpoint returns a JSON envelope (`page` member, escaped), so the parse found nothing and empty-esid entrymarks POSTs fired (they wrote zero rows — verified). (2) The retry omitted `all_students[]` → HTTP 500. (3) Two verification queries used the plural column `exam_group_class_batch_exams_id` (real: singular `exam_group_class_batch_exam_id`) and silently errored because DBQ() suppresses helper stderr — counts read as empty, not as errors. All three were diagnosed from artefacts/vendor code before any conclusion; no staging harm.
- **Unusual things:** `entrystudents` is a trap door — `Examstudent_model::add_student()` runs `array_diff($all_students, …)` on the raw post: omit `all_students[]` and PHP 8 throws a TypeError (0-byte 500); post it partially and the same call DELETES enrolments for roster students not selected. This is the same trap that cost BL-042F its R6e leg. Also: `addexamsubject` replaces the exam's WHOLE schedule grid per save (single-row posts overwrite each other); `payroll.php`'s staffattendance type map (absent=3) disagrees with this install's attendence_type table (3=Late, 4=Absent) — the lane seeded only types whose labels are unambiguous and never posted the field that arms the mail branches; and the "missing holiday table" was a naming mirage — the module's table is `annual_calendar`, present all along with 6 rows.
- **Lesson:** for vendor doors, read the model's write path before the first POST — the form's hidden fields (all_students[]) are load-bearing, and a door's success JSON is not proof until a correctly-named-column query reads the rows back. When a helper suppresses stderr, treat an empty count as an ERROR until a known-good query proves otherwise.

## Debrief #426 — oc29/oc30 payables consume-defect fix lane (Operqon, 2026-11-12 ~19:00–19:45 PKT)
- **Outcome:** PASS on staging. BL-EP-006 leg 3 proven end to end on the live repro: image oc30 `05d3208e5d56` (build log 23 PASS, 0 FAIL; in-image suites payables 46, gates 4, branding 15, refunds 22, services 47). Battery on oc30: maker pays Rs 60,000 against PPR-2026-00001 → Payment Entry ACC-PAY-2026-00009 submitted; proposal Paid with entry linked (owner maker slice10-accounts, decided_by distinct approver slice10-ta); second spend with fresh key refused INVALID_STATE (exactly-once); at-threshold without proposal refused; below-threshold replayed idempotently. Perms census: submit 0 everywhere, create 1 for the three seats, write 0 for Accounts User. Login probes byte-identical to oc26/27/28 baselines (Rektrs 37,058 / demo2 36,981 / Rams 37,101 B). Bench ends on oc30; oc29 retained as rollback; production untouched. BL-EP-006 ready to flip to TESTED (backlog bookkeeping is the parent's). Record team-oc29-payables-consume-fix.md §§1–8; contract bl-ep-006-contract.md gained an oc30 amendment section.
- **Mistakes:** (1) The oc29 re-seat fixed only the governed gate — the lane first declared the fix on the strength of the gate probe and the 45/45 suite, then the oc29 bench battery refused leg 3 with a bare PermissionError AFTER the entry posted (rolled back, no orphan). Layer 2 was `Document.save()` demanding `write` on the loaded proposal — no framework-checkable action can satisfy it, so a pure re-seat could never complete the consume. The lane should have live-probed the full save path (not just the gate) before calling the re-seat sufficient; the fake's `save()` checked nothing, so the suite could not catch it either. (2) The first `_save_doc` passed `ignore_permissions=` unconditionally, breaking the services suite's fake (`save()` takes no kwargs — 20 errors); fixed by using the kwarg form only when the flag is set. (3) The battery driver's snapshot helpers (`repro_state()`) read a module-level constant from inside a function — in `bench console` that name is undefined, so all START/END/repro snapshots failed (NameError) and had to be re-taken with top-level reads; the leg verdicts were unaffected. (4) The posture test's `.save(` ban tripped on new docstring wording and its carve-out count tripped on the docstring mentioning the flag — reworded/anchored.
- **Unusual things:** (1) The oc29 battery's leg-3a refusal was a bare `PermissionError` with an empty message — Frappe's own `raise frappe.PermissionError` with no message, at `Document.check_permission`; the empty message is itself the signature of a framework save-check refusal vs the governed layer's typed `OPERQON_WRITE:PERMISSION_DENIED`. (2) The oc29 swap loop died in a runtime restart after 2 refused attempts (attempts 1–2, 13:55–13:56 PKT) and was relaunched; both swaps then succeeded on attempt 1 via the proxy route, and the build/transfer legs also went first try — the egress spell had lifted by ~19:00 PKT. (3) `bench console` splits piped input so function bodies cannot see top-level names assigned in the same input (minimal probe reproduced: `NameError: name 'REPRO' is not defined` while module-level code worked) — a console quirk future bench drivers must design around. (4) The combined in-image suite run shows the documented fake-frappe sys.modules clash (134 tests, 1 failure + 43 errors); per-suite runs are the documented form and all pass.
- **Lesson:** a governed re-seat is proven only when the full mutation path is exercised live — the gate check and the persistence check are two different permission demands, and a fake that models one but not the other will stay green through exactly the layer it misses. Harden the fake at the same layer the live failure names, TDD the red first (the maker-pays test went red at exactly the live failure point), and keep the carve-out minimal, explicit, and posture-pinned to one call site. For bench drivers: never read a module constant from inside a helper — inline literals or pass values as arguments. The completion stayed inside option (i): `check_governed` untouched, DocType still non-submittable, payer still needs no `write`; the save carve-out is the mechanical persistence of an already-authorized governed command, with in-tree precedent (`access/enforcement.py:265`).
- **Resume action (CEO):** none for this lane. Carried: BL-EP-006 → TESTED flip in the backlog (parent bookkeeping); the oc29 battery driver's snapshot helpers still carry the console-scoping defect — the next lane reusing it should inline the repro reads.

## Debrief #427 — PF-2R3 sticky-header micro-fix lane (IQRS, 2026-11-12 ~19:24–19:37 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE + DEPLOYED on staging. Record `pixel-perfect/pf2r/PF2R-EXECUTION.md` §8. Diagnosis was evidence-led, not guessed: exhaustive census over every stylesheet the dashboard loads proved the ONLY non-visible overflow on any header ancestor was PF-2R2's own `.pk.pk-shell { overflow: clip }` on `.wrapper`, and that the vendor `.wrapper { overflow: hidden }` PF-2R2's §7.3 claimed to replace is not in the served cascade at all (AdminLTE.css linked by no shell view — §7.3's premise came from AdminLTE source, not the served cascade). Fix adopts the demo's own mechanism: fixed 60px bar (`position: fixed; top: 0; height: 60px`), `.pk.pk-shell { overflow: visible; padding-top: 60px }`, logo guard 44px. Deploy: 2 files (preskool-shell.css `fa2bfbf9…`, header.php `306b2d5b…`, stamp `?v=20261112-pf2r3`), on-host md5 2/2, BL-015 census IDENTICAL ×8, PF1-LINT PASS, smoke PASS, production untouched (header `c8bb6183…`). PIXEL-MATCH not claimed — CEO re-capture (scrolled dashboard) arbitrates.
- **Mistakes:** (1) §7.3's sticky premise was taken from vendor source rather than the served cascade — the lane had to re-derive the truth by census; the PF-2R2 record now carries a corrected premise, but the cost was a whole extra micro-fix round. (2) The PF-2R2 sticky rule was deployed unproven against a real scrolled render — the capture pass, not the deploy battery, caught it.
- **Unusual things:** the trapping rule was the lane's own predecessor's rule (`overflow: clip` from PF-2R2), not a vendor leftover — the fix removed a self-inflicted trap. The demo's header is fixed at exactly 60px, which made the fix a measurement, not a design choice.
- **Lesson:** verify CSS premises against the SERVED cascade (link lists from the live views + fetched files), never against library source on disk; and a sticky/fixed mechanism is only proven by a scrolled render, never by a static deploy battery. A micro-fix lane with a one-residual scope and a full census lands cleanly in ~13 minutes.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — CEO re-capture (scrolled dashboard) is the next step; the Addendum-3 round (charts/cards/top-4 wiring, byte-by-byte) is already running on the PF-2R3 base.

## Debrief #428 — PF-2R Leg S shell build leg, orphaned then closed (IQRS, 2026-11-12 ~18:56–19:33 PKT)
- **Outcome:** INTERRUPTED, no final report, work SUPERSEDED. Leg S (ed14699c, depth-2 child of the PF-2R addendum agent) was building the shell (header/sidebar) when its parent coordinator completed ~19:09 PKT without a final report; the completion lane audited the disk, found the shell CSS never existed (44 `pk2r-*` classes defined nowhere), and shipped its own shell CSS. Leg S's last transcript write was 18:56:39 PKT — a header/sidebar census + diff exec (132 orig PHP blocks vs 133 new, 52 missing/out-of-order, head section identical, CSRF 1/1) — mid-verification, no deploy, no report. It sat `pending_init`, quiet ~30 min (SUSPECT at the 19:26 inspector run); the inspector's wake nudge was scope-blocked twice (`subagent.send` refused — lane belongs to another chat's coordinator). CEO closed it via housekeeping instruction to the owning side chat ~19:33 PKT; the lane now reads `interrupted`.
- **Mistakes:** (1) When the first coordinator was replaced, no explicit close or re-home was issued for its live child — the orphan was discovered by the inspector, not by the handover. (2) The leg's own verification (the 18:56 census showing 52 missing/out-of-order PHP blocks) never reached a verdict — it was still mid-census when the parent died, so the shell-CSS hole was caught by the completion lane's audit instead.
- **Unusual things:** the leg's census output is genuinely useful forensic evidence (it documents exactly which vendor header blocks the PF-2R header dropped) even though the leg itself never reported — disk artefacts outlived the lane.
- **Lesson:** a coordinator handover must name the fate of every live child (close / re-home / keep) in the handover itself; an inspector cannot steer another chat's lanes (scope-blocked sends), so orphan closure has to go through the owning chat — the inspector's job is to name it and escalate, not to keep retrying a blocked send.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — Leg S's shell work is fully superseded by the deployed PF-2R/PF-2R2/PF-2R3 tree; its census output stays on disk as evidence only.

## Debrief #436 — PF-2R6 heatmap row-label micro-fix (IQRS, 2026-11-12 ~20:26–20:36 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE + DEPLOYED on staging. Record `pixel-perfect/pf2r/PF2R-EXECUTION.md` §11. 2 files, on-host md5 2/2, harness 136 PASS, PF1-LINT PASS, BL-015 census IDENTICAL ×8, stamp `?v=20261112-pf2r6`, backups in `~/pf2r6-backups-2026-11-12/`, production untouched. Root cause proven with numbers from the vendored library itself: ApexCharts v5.3.5 defaults `yaxis.labels.maxWidth: 160`, and its `conditionalChecksForAxisCoords` clamps the gutter to `min(max(natural, minWidth), 160)` — PF-2R5's minWidth-only fix (177) was nullified by the ceiling, gutter never exceeded 160 while the widest label needs 170.58px; `drawText` then ellipsised row 2 to exactly the string in the CEO crop ("Seven — Diamond (Hifz ...", reproduced character-for-character by the average-char-width math). First-glyph loss on both rows traced to Inter font-swap growth (+6.4/+7.9px vs fallback metrics, "F" = 7.08px, "S" = 7.70px). Fix: `minWidth == maxWidth == 185` (max(74, ⌈170.58⌉ + 14)) + chart render gated on `document.fonts.load('12px Inter')` with an 800 ms fallback and render-once guard.
- **Mistakes:** none in the deploy. The PF-2R5 lesson is closed by this lane: it measured against the exact served TTF with PIL and reproduced the CEO crop string exactly before fixing, instead of trusting harness geometry alone.
- **Unusual things:** the paint-order hop (font-swap timing) is stated as quantitatively consistent, not directly observed — the fix removes both the cap and the race so no variant survives; the CEO crop arbitrates. Deploy route direct rssh.sh, first-try connects throughout.
- **Lesson:** when a vendor library clamps your fix, read the library's own clamp order — setting only `minWidth` was silently nullified by the default `maxWidth` ceiling; pin both to the same computed width.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — the CEO browser crop re-proof arbitrates (labels must read in full, first characters present, no ellipsis); the running capture task (b737497c) is that leg.

## Debrief #445 — Operqon v3 Wave D, tenant ERP oc31 build + swap (coordinator-executed, 2026-11-12 ~21:20–21:40 PKT)

## Debrief #446 — Operqon v3 → Production MVP programme (coordinator lane, 2026-11-12 evening PKT)
- **Outcome:** Owner order (21:11 PKT: implement v3 directly on the Production MVP, pre-launch) executed across all three surfaces with per-surface backups/rollbacks. **Wave B Portal LIVE:** new apex release `v3portal-20261112-2126`, symlink repointed; v3 CF reskin of the customer portal (index rebuilt, dashboard/callback/verify/complete-signup link-only changes, all element IDs + scripts preserved, every JS file byte-identical), 8 honest sub-pages; guest battery 18/18 served hashes == pins; config.js preserved. **Wave D Tenant ERP LIVE:** bench oc31 `061aeea08dec` (Dreams ERP tokens + `#pos` DreamsPOS scope, build `v-7b76d4dde4a6`), governed api/ zero-diff, swap attempt 1 with worker preserved; logins 200 ×3, served token markers proven. **Wave C Console LIVE:** frontend-only release on mvp6, delta exactly one file `frontend/assets/console.css` (`5e9f4e1b…`, served sha == pin) reskinned to the CF language; gate 961 passed. **Wave A census + Wave E battery complete** — records `team-v3-prod-*.md` in the goal workspace.
- **Mistakes:** (1) oc31 build launcher failed blind ~15 min: no `mkdir -p` for the VPS target parent + sync stderr suppressed (`2>/dev/null`) — NOT egress; fixed with one mkdir + one open-stderr attempt. (2) Console deploy attempt 1 false-failed AFTER a clean install+gate on a never-passable acceptance check (`/tenants.html` = 200 without following the S5 clean-URL 301), and the auto-rollback's copy of the same check false-failed its (actually correct) file restore AND its exit skipped the timer-resume line, leaving the provisioner timer inactive until the coordinator restarted it manually. Both scripts patched to assert the final code with `-L` under dated harness-correction notes; attempt 2 all-PASS. (3) Wave D record PKT timestamps ran ahead of the real clock (inspector-flagged, #445); Wave C/E records use box-clock UTC.
- **Unusual things:** the local portal tree (`frontend-apex`) was stale vs live on EVERY customer file — caught by hash comparison before composing; the byte-exact live tree was pulled and used as base (its own bundled MANIFEST was stale too). The v3 design's `console/overview.html` is a corrupt 70 MB fragment (sidebar repeated ×12,971, no doctype) — reconstructed in the stage tree (9,071 B, honest empty states), not published. Publishing the v3 console static pages at all was evidence-stopped: nginx serves FRONT files to guests via try_files (auth is client-side OIDC), the shipped CSP blocks their inline styles/fonts, and 10 of 21 pages have no provider endpoint (blockers B-1…B-5 recorded) — the honest Wave C was the SPA reskin, not the mock pages. The ERP lane caught a silent re-fixturing trap (canonical config "fixture" vs oc30's shipped "live" snapshot) — shipped config verified byte-identical to oc30's.
- **Lesson:** hash-compare every carried subtree against LIVE before composing (local trees lie); a check that can never pass is a harness defect — read the wire (301 + final bytes) before calling a deploy failed, and order rollback scripts so timers resume before any check that can exit; launchers must `mkdir -p` targets and never suppress sync stderr; demo data in design mockups is never publishable — scrub to real wiring or honest empty states, and stop the part whose backend doesn't exist instead of faking the surface.
- **Resume action (CEO):** one bookkeeping item — GitHub snapshot push of `release-v3-console/` + RELEASES.md receipt, then advance the provider marker from C7 (flagged in the Wave C record; needs the connector/approval route). Final act 00:32: lane edited `tools-bl133/bl133_schema.php` (sidebar INSERT changed: menu 15→1, level 3→2, menu/key blanked) and `bl133_dbw.php` (sidebar_258 check relaxed from `id = 258 AND lang_key` to lang_key-only), then launched a 12-try direct-route exec (timeout 90, sleep 6) to upload both scripts and run schema + counts — the exec never returned an output item. Hosts proven fine by the inspector at 00:41 (staging 200 in 1.79s, production 200 in 1.78s) — not a host stall.
- **Mistakes:** (a) the sidebar verification loop burned 11+ no-window tries over ~20 min before the lane changed tactic at 00:32; (b) the record was last written 00:09 PKT (§3), so the 00:09–00:34 work (DBW upload, verification retries, both 00:32 edits, final exec) exists only in the transcript (seq 28158–28163); (c) the final exec's 180s yield + 12-try loop left the agent inside one long exec with no checkpoint write when the interruption hit.
- **Unusual things:** both SSH routes hit CONNECT-refusal spells at different points in the same lane (jump mid-lane, direct for the sidebar verification); the sidebar insert carried a hardcoded id expectation (258) that the lane itself then had to relax to a lang_key check — the insert may have landed under a different id, or not at all.
- **Lesson:** after ~5 no-window tries on a verification probe, change the check or the route immediately instead of retrying the same failing probe; and write a record checkpoint BEFORE launching a long retry exec, so an interruption mid-exec does not leave the last 25 min unrecorded.
- **Resume action (CEO):** close lane ceaed01a; dispatch a state-preflight resume lane — (1) read transcript tail seq 28158–28163 + the 00:32-edited `tools-bl133` scripts; (2) verify on staging FIRST whether the schema re-run landed (sidebar row `payroll_governance` present? which id?) and whether Set 1b `Pk_payroll_lib` (`728d8401…`) is live — do NOT re-run schema blindly; (3) finish sidebar verification + post-checks (root mode, 750 count, counts, mapcheck); (4) run the BL-133 battery; (5) write record §4+ and a ≤15-line final report. No nudge was sent — an interrupted agent cannot be nudged back; redispatch is the CEO's.

The one FAIL (E3) was a REAL defect, fixed in-lane as **Set 1c**: vendor admin header renders no controller flashdata, so refusal messages were invisible — flash banner now rendered in the controller's shared `render()` path (`admin/Pkpayroll` `951452b8…` → `3733e418…`, lint PASS); **re-proof 7/7 PASS**. (b) The GitHub push approval card sat pending 03:42 → 08:11 PKT (~4.5 h) and was finally **Allowed 08:11:15 PKT**; the retry raised a second card (requested 08:09:27, Allowed 08:11:19) — either approval unblocked the push; it landed as `b3f10153…` minutes later. (c) The ~2.5 h "quiet" (03:42–06:02) stacked TWO independent causes — a pending approval card AND a restart-killed exec — so transcript silence alone did not explain the stall; the inspector had to check both. (d) Staging showed the **000/~10.6 s host-stall signature twice** at the 08:11 inspector probe while production answered 200 in 1.79 s — a fresh stall spell starting around the push landing, unrelated to the lane (the push touched GitHub only).

For the inspector: a long quiet can stack two causes (pending card + killed exec) — check both before classifying.

## Debrief #457 — BL-046 + BL-047 Front Office + Communicate lane (IQRS, 2026-11-13 ~08:2x–11:26 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE (staging only). Lane f880b37f ran ~3h. Shipped: Front Office workspace (`admin/pkfrontoffice` — gate/exit passes on the BL-063 triple check, visitor verification, appointments queue) + Communicate workspace (`admin/pkcommunicate` — one-record notices, notification-centre view, schedule log + cancel, WhatsApp not-configured boundary, chat, calendar, to-do/notes) + portal appointments (`user/appointments`, own-children only); 2 libs, 3 controllers, 14 views, CSS block, stamp `?v=20261113-bl046`, 4 tables + 7 policy keys. Battery runs 1–4: 54/13, 74/2, 80/1, **81 PASS / 0 FAIL** — every failure diagnosed. Guards at close: exam-19 fingerprint exact, pins 1570, staff back to 122, fee census 2646→2646, proof accounts deleted + credentials refused, production untouched. Snapshot: entry 31, commit `aa0b450d…` on `asadchoudharry/iqrs-system` main, remote-verified (record reads back from main). Final report delivered (transcript seq 29575).
- **Mistakes:** (a) **The lane misdiagnosed its own blocker for ~2 hours.** V1 died 09:42 on menuseed after 40 tries, V2 died 10:44 after 120 tries (~55 min) — both blamed on the SSH/egress-proxy refusal spell. The real cause was a code bug: `bl046_dbw.php:180` `bind_param('issssss')` — 7 type chars for 6 variables/placeholders, PHP 8 ValueError, silent on host. Menuseed could never have succeeded on any route. Fixed in-lane to `'isssss'`; deploy then completed by hand in the open window 10:56–10:58 PKT. (b) **Three real app defects shipped in the first build and were only caught by the battery:** communicate index redirect, lowercase `yes`/`no` vs vendor `Yes`/`No`, and workspace flash messages never rendered anywhere (controllers set flashdata on every POST, no view rendered it). (c) Battery run 1's 13 failures included 5 vacuous passes (C7, E7, F10, G13, H1) — named in the record and re-proven in run 2. (d) Run 2's 2 failures were one battery bug: a fixture-identity mix-up (parent 7396 owns child 3699; 3752/3753 belong to parent 7458) — the app's own/foreign enforcement was proven correct by the inversion. (e) Run 3's single failure was a battery assertion bug (E6 grepped `<tr>` for a `data-student-id` that lives on the `<td>`).
- **Unusual things:** (a) **V3 driver died silently ~05:49–05:53Z with no STEP-FAILED line** — hash-upload and set-1 DONE in an admission window, then the driver vanished before the first menuseed try; no processes remained. Likely cause: the runtime reaped the process tree of the output-drained launcher exec (`proc_5dcba5f7dbce` reported `subprocess.output_drain_timeout` at launch). The deploy did not depend on the driver surviving — remaining steps were run by hand. (b) **A 342 KB unthrottled stdin burst broke the proxy** (`BlockingIOError`, broken pipe); the redeploy went through throttled at ~160 KB/s (16 KB/0.1 s). (c) `make_deploy.py` gates ABSENT-baseline files as SKIP-iff-current==NEW-build else ABORT — a changed build ABORTs; spec baselines had to be set to the deployed old-build md5s before regenerating. (d) Staging showed the known 000/~10 s host-stall signature at lane start and the SSH refusal spell ran ~2.5 h, overlapping the real code bug — two independent causes stacked in one stall, and the route explanation masked the code one.
- **Lesson:** when a step fails identically across every route and retry, read the failing step's own code before blaming the transport — a silent PHP ValueError looks exactly like a network refusal from the outside; and a driver that vanishes mid-step with no failure line is a reaped process tree, not a completed step — launch drivers so the launcher exec exits cleanly. For the inspector: a long quiet can stack a transport spell AND a code bug — check the step's own failure mode, not just the route.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none for BL-046/047 — done. Next per D-037: **BL-108**. Tails: in-workspace chat send unwired; vendor list views go to PF-4/5; WhatsApp stays not-configured; portal layout flash invisible; `.pw-parent` retained (mode 600).

Apply materialises exactly ONE file (`preskool-theme-active.css`) — tokens.css never written, no per-theme view edits. Battery run 1 = **43 PASS / 10 FAIL** (every failure named — battery flaws + cascades), run 2 re-proof **16/17 + manual login-stamp re-proof**; **neutrality 0 diffs / 32,662 declarations** under the default package; violet proof theme re-resolved 1,220 declarations; **rollback exact (theme md5 == default md5)**; print marksheet byte-identical under default; all refusal classes zero-write; guards exact (census 122, pins 1570, masters 2646, deposits 1570, BL-134's 10 findings, exam-19 fingerprint, ROOT 755/DIRS750=0); production absence proven. Snapshot: **sync entry 39, commit `4299a76248be`**, remote-verified by CEO. Final report delivered ~20:52 PKT.
- **Mistakes:** (a) Two in-lane defects found before run 1 and fixed: the lib's `parse_scopes` skipped MIXED blocks entirely, dropping the live `body` block's `--bs-body-font-family` from the contract — rule corrected (mixed blocks contribute var defs; purity enforced on packages only); the writer's `policy_set` used a wrong `pk_policy_keys` shape and the census pin moved from `census_json` (cannot fit varchar(120)) to `policy.theme.census_md5`. (b) Battery typos: B-structure ×2 expected `TOKEN_STRUCTURE` while the lib's code is `TOKENS_STRUCTURE` (refusal behaviour itself correct); C6 writer census port used a `{hex,rgb,px}` shape while the lib returns `{hex_total, hex_distinct, fn_colour}`. (c) Battery sequence error: the D9 chain rolled back to the overrides package, not preskool — the D9a leg asserted only the OK code, **vacuous, named as such** — leaving the wrong theme active for every downstream leg.

(c) The seed row's validation report is stamped at first apply by design.
- **Lesson:** a battery leg that asserts only the OK code is vacuous — assert the resulting state (which theme is active), not the return code; and a rollback chain that lands on the wrong package poisons every downstream leg — re-prove from a known state. Also: recon must read the real schema (`pk_policy_keys` shape) before the writer is written, not after the first battery run.

## Debrief #479 — PF-4/5 Lane B3 pkstudents Export dropdown fix (IQRS, 2026-11-13 ~23:56–23:59 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE + DEPLOYED to staging (record `pf45/PF45-LANE-B3-EXECUTION.md`). Root cause PROVEN, not guessed: the menu items were in the DOM at `display:none` — PF-1's `preskool-components.css` `.pk .dropdown-menu{display:none}` (0,2,0) tied BS3's `.open>.dropdown-menu{display:block}` and won on link order, and the students head sat outside every scoped restore (shell restores only under `.main-header`/`.main-sidebar`; PF-2R5's only under `.pk-dash .pkr-head-actions`; Lane A2's only under `.pk-fee-workspace`). Fix: one appended block in `preskool-shell.css` (43 lines, 0 changed) scoped `.pk-stu-workspace .pk-page-actions`, carrying the working fees block's values verbatim, plus cache-buster stamp. Proofs: served CSS 78,930 B byte-identical with the new rule at L2008; on-host md5 2/2; modes 755/644; anonymous gates 307 ×5; BL-015 auth views byte-identical; production untouched (sentinels identical). Backups on-host `~/backups-pf45b3-20261114/`.
- **Mistakes:** none in this lane. It did what B2's verification could not: proved the cause on the deployed file (host md5 == B2 build) before fixing, and ruled out the markup and JS hypotheses with evidence.
- **Unusual things:** (a) Same disease as PF-2R5 §10.1, third surface — the latent break awaits every future workspace head rendering a BS3 dropdown inside `.content-wrapper` without a scoped restore (pkexams/pkacademics/pkattendance/pkhr); B3 named it so those lanes price it in. (b) The capture tool's "no Export as text" counts rendered items only — the `<li>`s were present but hidden, which is why the defect looked like missing markup.
- **Lesson:** when a menu renders empty, check the deployed CSS cascade before the markup — a specificity tie decided by link order hides items that are provably in the DOM. And a scoped restore must travel with every workspace head that uses a BS3 dropdown, not live in one workspace's sheet.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none for Lane B3 — done; the post-fix re-capture (debrief #481) proved the fix live. Open tails carried forward: signed-in export downloads cross-footed against the screen (XLSX 5 KB downloaded in the re-capture; PDF/CSV still to be cross-footed); CEO paired-capture PIXEL-MATCH verdict for pkstudents.

## Debrief #489 — PF-4/5 Lane D2, attendance calendar band fills (IQRS, 2026-11-14 ~00:12–00:20 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETED + deployed to staging — the register month calendar's marked-day cells now show visible band fills (5/9 Nov royal blue, 6 Nov pale blue, unmarked pale grey), proven by CEO re-capture ~00:20 PKT.

Fix: the 5 band rules in `preskool-attendance.css` now carry `background-color:var(--token)!important` at higher specificity (stamp `?v=20261114-pf45d2`).

- **Resume action (CEO):** none — lane done; text-colour follow-up rode Lanes D3/D4.

## Debrief #490 — PF-4/5 Lane D3, attendance deep-band white text (IQRS, 2026-11-14 ~00:21–00:27 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETED + deployed to staging, then REFUTED by CEO signed-in re-capture ~00:27 PKT — day number and "100.0%" on b4 cells still dark navy; the lane's "computes 5.40:1" claim was wrong.
- **Mistakes:** fixed the colour on the td, but every text node in the cell sits inside an inner `<a>` whose own components rule `.pk .table tbody tr td a{color:…}` (0,2,4) wins over the td fix; the 5.40:1 figure was a contrast computation over declared values, not a rendered result. The lane's §1 model ("link inherits the td's muted ink") was factually wrong — the link never inherits the td's colour.
- **Unusual things:** D3's td-level fix genuinely worked on the td itself (rendered white on the cell) yet changed no glyph — a fix can be provably correct on the wrong element. Dated correction line added to D3's record §3a; history not rewritten.
- **Lesson:** a computed-style claim is NOT proof — only a rendered capture arbitrates; and a fix must be scoped to the element that actually carries the text, traced with rendered-DOM evidence.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none for D3 — Lane D4 (diagnose-then-fix with CDP matched-rules trace) dispatched on the refutation.

## Debrief #491 — PF-4/5 Lane D4, attendance deep-band text rendered-cascade fix (IQRS, 2026-11-14 ~00:27–00:38 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETED + deployed to staging (md5 8/8, modes 755/644, production untouched) — CDP matched-rules trace on the CEO's captured served page proved the winner: components L2464 `.pk .table tbody tr td a` (0,2,4) over the link; spans inherit from the link, never the td. Element-level grouped rule (b3/b4 link + day + pct, white `!important`) added; rendered after-proof shows b4/b3 link/day/pct all rgb(255,255,255). CEO final gate capture ~00:39 PKT confirmed bold white text live — ATTENDANCE CLOSED.
- **Mistakes:** none — the lane did exactly what D3 skipped: reproduced the CEO's page in a real browser engine with the deployed sheet bytes, and verified in a render, not by computation.
- **Unusual things:** the D2→D4 chain is the wave's cascade lesson in miniature: bootstrap `!important` white-wash on td backgrounds (D2), then a components link rule (0,2,4) beating every td-level text fix (D4). The `:hover` sibling at (0,3,4) forced the `!important` on the fix — a plain descendant rule would have lost on hover.
- **Lesson:** when a fix "computes right but renders wrong", run `CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode` on the captured served page — the matched-rule list names the winner; guessing from the sheet never does.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — lane done, workspace closed.

## Debrief #504 — Desktop D2-6 battery run 22 (IQRS, 2026-11-14 ~15:25–15:47 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE as a run, phase A 40/40 ALL PASS (second consecutive full phase-A pass), driver DB proofs 20/20 ALL PASS — the L1/L2 id-scoping fix from run 21 is proven (max id at start 24). Phase B 1/5 again, but the cause is now FOUND and fixed: a battery-harness defect, not the route. `phaseDeadlineMs` was armed only at the top of `phaseA`; `phaseB` never set it, so in phase B's JVM the deadline was 0 and every `deliver()` stopped instantly ("phase budget spent" on the first push of every B leg). Phase B never ran before run 21 (phase A never passed), so the defect stayed hidden. Fix: arm `phaseDeadlineMs` at the top of `phaseB` too; recompiled into `build/classes`. Run 23 (gated job `tools-d2r/clean-run23.sh`) is the first run that can honestly pass phase B.
- **Mistakes:** runs 21 and 22 both misread phase B's failures as route fallout — the evidence was in the deliver NOTEs all along ("phase budget spent" on first push), and a route death would have shown retries dying on network EOF, not an instant stop. The lane corrected its own reading in the run-22 write-up.
- **Unusual things:** a deadline armed in one phase and silently zero in the next is a class of bug that only surfaces when the earlier phase finally passes — the harness's own gating hid it for 20 runs.
- **Lesson:** when a leg fails instantly with no retries spent, read the failure's own reason string before blaming the network — "budget spent on first push" is a harness bug signature, not a transport signature.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — run 23 already launched by the lane on the fixed harness; D2-6 continues.

## Debrief #505 — Desktop Lane D2-R (D2-6 Remaining Screens) ENDS (IQRS, 2026-11-14 ~16:19 PKT)
- **Outcome:** lane ENDED (runtime "completed", NO final report) after ~13.75 h. Build COMPLETE (21 screens, record §35; local proof 14/14, gallery 28/28, snapshot gate green, zero server files changed). Battery §5.2-R runs 18–23: run 21 = first full phase A (40/40); run 22 = phase A 40/40 + DB proofs 20/20 (first fully clean pass through the proofs); phase-B harness defect found + fixed in run 22; run 23 KILLED mid-phase-A (26 PASS, last leg A-I2) by a runtime restart ~16:05 PKT. The lane's last acts (record write 16:19:33, 7 s before it ended) recorded run 23 and launched a DETACHED cleanup + run-24 job (`tools-d2r/clean-run24.sh`, setsid/nohup) so the battery survives without the lane. D2-6 CLOSE-OUT NOT done (no §44 final/§45, proof staff 276 still live, lane key not revoked, census not back to 122) — carried to the CEO's resume lane.
- **Mistakes:** (1) the sshq wrapper greps for `"k"`/`"v"` keys the cleanfixture JSON lacks, so EXECUTED deletes read as "empty tries" for hours — runs 19/20 cleanup confusion and run 20 launching on a dirty baseline followed from it; (2) phase-B failures misread as route fallout in runs 21/22 when the "phase budget spent" signature was in the deliver NOTEs all along (owned + corrected in the run-22 write-up); (3) a /tmp overlay was trusted across a runtime restart (the ~06:45 "Unauthorized" root cause) — fixed by rebuilding the overlay at every start.
- **Unusual things:** the lane ended "completed" with no summary — its durable record and the detached job table were the ground truth, not a final message; the setsid/nohup detached-job pattern is a new survival mechanism for battery work across runtime restarts (run 10 was also SIGTERM-killed by a restart, and the run-21 watch job died the same way).
- **Lesson:** a lane's continuity lives in its record + detached jobs, never in its session — battery drivers must not depend on /tmp or on the lane staying alive, and a lane that ends without a report is closed out from its record, not from memory.
- **Resume action (CEO):** resume lane (D2-R2) dispatched ~16:2x PKT to supervise clean-run24 → run 24 and complete the D2-6 close-out (or iterate runs until a full clean run lands).

## Debrief #517 — Full audit lane, IQRS Android apps (IQRS, 2026-11-15 ~08:24–08:31 PKT)

## Debrief #518 — Print-parity check lane, IQRS Android apps (IQRS, 2026-11-15 ~08:38–08:41 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE — §7 appended to MOBILE-AUDIT-2026-11-15.md (§7.1–7.4) plus a B6 pointer in the §6 blocker list; no code changed. 22 print/document outputs inventoried: A server-rendered 12 (9 generated documents — 8× A⚠ + 1× A◐ — plus CSV and stored-file openings), B app-rendered 3 (family fee-receipt sheet, staff fee-receipt screen copy, staff payslip sheet with no server door at all), C on-screen-only 7. Key finding: even the server-rendered documents breach the owner's print rule on a second layer — Familydocs/Staffapi render PDFs from their own private inline HTML (text-only navy letterhead, no crest/footer/signature/print.css) and never invoke the unified web producers; the ID-card PDFs are bare text with the QR printed as a literal string, versus the web's designed CARD-profile document. B6-1…B6-5 recorded (app sheets, all A⚠ kinds, certificate background loss).
- **Mistakes:** none recorded.
- **Unusual things:** the breach is two-layered (app layer + API layer) — "server-rendered" was assumed to mean compliant, but server-rendered ≠ web-design; the API controllers carry a private copy of a mini print layer that is a third design, neither the app's nor the web's. The certificate template's background image is explicitly dropped server-side (`background_applied:false`).
- **Lesson:** "server-rendered" is not proof of design parity — trace the document to the actual producer; a private copy of a print layer inside an API controller stays invisible until you read the controller.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — lane done; the B6 fix lane (re-render A⚠ kinds through the unified producers + retire/replace the app sheets) follows; the B7 role-awareness check lane is now running.

## Debrief #520 — QR scanner speed fix lane, IQRS Workspace app (IQRS, 2026-11-15 ~08:47–08:55 PKT)
- **Outcome:** COMPLETE — record QR-SCANNER-FIX-2026-11-15.md. Diagnosis (from the code): the confirmation waited on a full server roundtrip before showing the green name card (offline fallback was a hard-coded 6,000 ms delay), TRY_HARDER ran on every decode attempt, upright failures rotated the full 1280×720 brightness plane both ways (up to 3 full decodes + two ~921k-element buffer copies per frame), and there was no beep or haptic anywhere. Fix: frame → cheap passes (centre crop first) → code → in-memory session decision → write saved to the existing offline outbox immediately (idempotent client txn id, as before) + green card with the student's name from the local roster/daybook + beep + buzz, all in the same frame cycle, network not involved; 3 s per-code hold at decoder and session level; re-scan shows an amber "Already marked present" card with a lower tone and writes nothing; server refusals still surface as the plain-words attention card with the write held on Waiting. Only Torch, manual-entry Mark and Done buttons remain in the loop. Proof: ./tools/run_tests.sh OK (371 tests = 352 baseline + 13 QrScanSessionTest + 6 QrDecoderTest, 0 failures); ./build.sh both clean (Workspace APK +4,096 B, Connect ±0 — scanner ships only in Workspace); banned-strings + metadata gates pass; JVM decoder micro-benchmark 12→9 ms blank frame, 2→1 ms small code (relative evidence only, not device timing). Scope honoured: app-side QR/attendance files only, no server change, the parallel B6 lane's files untouched; the B7-1 Scan caps gate was explicitly NOT done (separate pending owner decision). Production untouched.
- **Mistakes:** none recorded.
- **Unusual things:** the record honestly flags real-world device verification as unproven (detection speed under school lighting, beep audibility, focus on low/mid-range phones) and claims nothing from VM evidence — the right call, since decoder micro-benchmarks on a 1.5-vCPU VM are not device timing.
- **Lesson:** the perceived slowness was a feedback problem, not a decode problem — confirm locally first and reconcile with the server after, instead of making the teacher wait on the network to see a scan land.
- **Resume action (CEO):** none — lane done; device verification rides the owner's phone pass when he installs the build.

Record: MOBILE-PRINT-FIX-2026-11-15.md (§4–§6); proof PDFs fetched + poppler-verified.

Root cause was the api tree's slim Setting_model lacking `getAdminlogo()` (web model has it); remedy = port that one method verbatim from the web model into the staging api tree (11,539 B / `23b4d0c1…` → 11,733 B / `b7f0d5ae…`, method block only, `php -l` clean). The inspector's wake-nudge attempt for that failure was BLOCKED — the lane is owned by another chat, outside direct `subagent.send` scope — no nudge was delivered, and none was needed.

Domain ownership already verified from the setup lane.

- **Unusual things:** nothing in the work itself was unfinished — the recovery lane's only repair was reverting a leftover temp override before commit.
- **Lesson:** commit + report are part of done, not afterthoughts; a build lane that ends silent forces a recovery lane and costs a full inspector cycle. Lanes must commit before their last step and always leave a final response.
- **Resume action (CEO):** Slice 4 committed as `1ffe3992` (local only — push state unverifiable from this VM, GitHub auth unavailable here); push + production train follows the Slice 3 pattern (push lane → workflow edit → build → GHCR config verify → swap → Dokploy-side pin update).

- **Outcome:** COMPLETE — the D1 UpgradeCode was read on the laptop and ADOPTED: `{D03044A1-54E3-3B50-B417-3A9BE021B9F4}` (laptop-read, NOT the frozen fallback `c40234e1-…`). The D1 install's upgrade chain is preserved. W0 gate closed.
- **Mistakes:** none evident.
- **Unusual things:** The frozen fallback UpgradeCode would have broken the upgrade chain if adopted blindly — the laptop read was the only correct source, and it worked because the owner had the laptop ON (09:45 order) and the lapssh StrictHostKeyChecking fix had landed.

## Debrief #581 — Cursor CONTINUE-nudge + Dreams Core full-build prompt browser tasks c6c603b5 / 556b93b6 (Operqon/Cursor, 2026-11-16 ~09:4x–09:5x PKT)
- **Outcome:** FAILED (blocked, not a lane error) — neither the three CONTINUE nudge messages nor the complete Dreams Core full-build prompt reached Cursor. Cause: Cursor agent is on its WEEKLY usage limit — panel banner "Weekly usage limit reached. It resets in 4 days. Buy credits to keep going now, or upgrade your plan." Five send attempts rejected; composer draft restored each time; transcript unchanged at 113 messages; last Cursor work 2026-11-15 22:23 PKT.
- **Mistakes:** none by the tasks — the limit is a hard wall, and the tasks correctly stopped instead of posting duplicates.
- **Unusual things:** (1) Nothing was lost: the full prompt sits verbatim as a draft in the Cursor chat composer, sendable in one click once usage is restored (credits/upgrade or the weekly reset). (2) This is the second Cursor outage in the loop (first: limit exhausted ~22:28 PKT 2026-11-15, reset ~19 Nov) — the "resets in 4 days" banner now points at ~20 Nov. (3) The S3 landing run3 + S1+S2+S3 production deploy do NOT depend on Cursor (Muse owns merges under the owner's 00:09 order), so the Operqon deploy path is unaffected — only the Cursor-executed build loop is parked.
- **Lesson:** a usage-limit wall is not a retry problem — do not burn send attempts against it; park the prompt as a draft and wait for credits/reset. Report the blocker once, plainly, with the owner-only step named (buy credits / upgrade / wait).
- **Resume action (CEO):** S3 lander (run3, PID 2038558 on-host) running; production deploy follows landing. Cursor loop resumes only when the owner buys credits/upgrades or the limit resets (~4 days). Do NOT re-type or re-send a second copy of the prompt meanwhile.
